title: Senior Account Sales Manager
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Senior Account Sales Manager is responsible for leading a high-performing sales team to understand customer technology, product, and business strategies, building partnerships from engineering teams to executive leadership, and securing strategic design wins in close collaboration with engineering and cross-functional teams. This role drives account planning and execution, ensuring alignment with both customer priorities and Intel’s long-term growth objectives.

The position actively identifies, develops, and accelerates new revenue streams, converting design wins into billed revenue (sales in and/or sales through), while expanding Intel’s global product portfolio for adoption across regional markets. It gathers and analyzes customer feedback at all levels—from engineers to executives—to enhance satisfaction, mitigate risks, and implement recovery actions that strengthen customer loyalty.

By influencing customer decisions and enabling sales execution, the Senior Account Sales Manager ensures both immediate business results and sustainable long-term growth.

This is a commissioned senior sales position, directly tied to revenue generation, customer success, and strategic business expansion.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in business, Engineering, or a related field
  • 8~15 years of experience in B2B and/or technology sales
  • Strong account management and relationship building skills
  • Solid understanding of the IT market and ecosystem
  • Proven ability to drive revenue, manage sales pipeline, and close deals
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills
  • Ability to work effectively in a global, matrix organization
  • Fluent in English
  • Native level Japanese
  • Willingness to travel as required


Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience in an Account Manager or Account Sales Manager role
  • Experience managing large or strategic enterprise accounts

title: Sr. Substrates Development and Ramp Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

  • Supports management/senior leadership to incorporate process and quality improvements in Intel's supply chain and logistics strategy.

  • Defines material inspection methodology, conducts studies related to cost control, process control, and production yield, and implements plans and programs to optimize supply chain.

title: AI Performance Library Architect
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Software and AI (SAI) organization is looking for a software development engineer to work on oneDNN project ( https://github.com/uxlfoundation/oneDNN ). oneDNN is a complex cross-platform open-source software project focusing on neural network performance. oneDNN is a critical and highly visible component of Intel AI strategy, powering key AI applications including OpenVINO, Tensorflow, Pytorch, ONNX Runtime, and more. In this role, you will be responsible for design, development, and maintenance of new functionality in oneDNN to enable performance critical portions of AI workloads. In this role you will be supporting software developers optimizing AI frameworks and workloads for Intel CPUs and GPUs, as well as cross-platform ecosystem of AI software developers contributing to oneDNN.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

Minimum requirements:

  • Master’s degree in Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, or a relevant STEM field. OR
  • Ph.D. degree in Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, or a relevant STEM field.
  • 5+ years of experience in the following areas:
    • C and C++
    • Maintaining or contributing to open-source software projects
    • Software libraries design and architecture
    • Implementation of linear algebra algorithms (functions from BLAS, LAPACK, or PyTorch)
    • Performance engineering and software performance optimizations
    • Floating point arithmetic and numerical stability
    • Software development on Linux
    • Low-level performance optimizations using CUDA, x86 assembly or intrinsics, or OpenCL

Preferred qualifications:

  • 3 years+ Machine learning and deep learning algorithms or High-performance computing (HPC) applications development
  • 3 year+ Floating point implementations of transcendental functions (sin, cos, tanh, elu, etc)
  • 1 year+ Algorithms for non-IEEE low precision data types (bfloat16, fp8, fp4)
  • 1 year+ AI assisted software development

Requirements listed would be obtained through a combination of industry relevant job experience, internship experiences and/or schoolwork/classes/research.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Embark with us on a journey of growth and transformation as we create exceptionally engineered technology and bring AI everywhere. As a valued team member, your adaptability and attention to detail will contribute to our drive for results and relentless pursuit of quality, ensuring we meet our customers' needs with precision.

Join us and build on our legacy of innovation and collaboration as we deliver world‑changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet.

Life at Intel: https://jobs.intel.com/en/life-at-intel

We are seeking a highly motivated and technically skilled Integrator to lead the development and execution of new product/ process introduction and process transfers across factories.

The ideal candidate will play a key role in ensuring that technology, platforms, and products meet certification requirements before transferring to HVM.
 
The NPI integrator will be responsible for but not limited to:

  • Tracking the collateral items, communicating wafer shipping to post fab customers, creating and updating the product codes in the internal systems.
  • Setting up lot flows, kicking off NPI Checklists for each module, starting the silicon and monitoring its progress through the process flow for set up, power-on and engineering samples until first production.
  • Develop and implement new NPI systems and business processes as they become ready and close any issues identified in a NPI reflection

 
The candidate should exhibit the following behavioral traits:

  • Candidates are expected to have strong understanding of a product’s life cycle, fab processing, and post fab activities.

title: Senior Wet Etch Manufacturing Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Shape the Future of Semiconductor Manufacturing at Intel

Join Intel's newest and most innovative organization—Manufacturing Development Customer Engineering (MDCE)—where you'll bridge the critical gap between breakthrough technology development and high-volume manufacturing. As a Senior Wet Etch Manufacturing Development Engineer, you'll be at the forefront of advancing next-generation semiconductor technologies that power the world's most sophisticated devices.

Organization Impact

MDCE represents Intel's strategic evolution within Intel Foundry Technology Manufacturing (FTM). We're the vital link that transforms cutting-edge research into manufacturable reality, advancing technology nodes from initial qualification to high-yield production while delivering enhanced solutions for foundry customers worldwide.

Your Role in Technology Leadership

Drive technology innovation that defines Intel's future roadmap while enabling advanced manufacturing processes that set industry standards. You'll develop next-generation device architectures, support high-volume production scaling, and collaborate with world-class suppliers to deliver breakthrough solutions that maintain Intel's semiconductor leadership.

Direct Impact

Your innovations will power billions of devices globally, ensuring Intel's continued dominance in delivering world-class silicon solutions that push the boundaries of what's technologically possible.

Core Responsibilities

Advanced Process Development

  • Lead design, development, and optimization of sophisticated manufacturing processes
  • Drive parameter optimization, material selection, and system design to exceed functional requirements
  • Conduct feasibility studies using theoretical simulations and practical engineering methodologies
  • Enable innovative device architectures that define next-generation semiconductor capabilities

Strategic Technology Leadership

  • Develop comprehensive technology roadmaps for future manufacturing processes
  • Identify and pursue opportunities to advance Intel's process capabilities
  • Conduct pathfinding activities aligned with industry trends and customer requirements
  • Integrate emerging technologies into Intel's manufacturing ecosystem

Manufacturing Excellence

  • Implement equipment modifications to enhance production efficiency and reduce defects
  • Drive complex problem-solving initiatives for defect reduction and yield improvement
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders and external suppliers on critical enabling technologies
  • Ensure seamless integration across etch, deposition, CMP, and lithography modules

Innovation & Continuous Improvement

  • Stay current with industrial trends and breakthrough technologies
  • Apply disciplined execution and data-driven problem-solving methods
  • Lead root-cause analysis using structured approaches and advanced analytics
  • Drive solutions from concept through factory implementation

Operational Excellence

  • Ability to thrive in fast-paced, dynamic environments
  • Commitment to maintaining highest standards of safety, quality, and compliance
  • Experience with advanced foundry customer requirements and specifications

Qualifications:

The Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position.  Minimum qualifications listed below would be obtained through a combination of industry relevant job experience, internship experience and / or schoolwork/classes/research. The preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, Mechanical Engineering, or in a STEM related field
  • 7+ years of semiconductor manufacturing, process development, or technology development experience
  • 1+ years of experience in Design of Experiments (DOE) and statistical process control
  • 2+ years of experience in root-cause analysis capabilities using structured problem-solving and data analytics.
  • 2+ years of experience with module integration and interactions across semiconductor processes including; etch, deposition, CMP, or lithography.
  • Experience in process optimization, defect reduction, and manufacturing improvements
  • Hands-on experience with advanced manufacturing processes (e.g. etching, material science, and/or equipment metrology)

Preferred Qualifications

  • Post Graduate degree in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, Mechanical Engineering, or in a STEM related field
  • Experience with cutting-edge technology nodes (sub-10nm logic or leading-edge foundry nodes)
  • Proven track record collaborating with equipment and materials suppliers
  • Cross-functional leadership experience leading task forces for yield improvements and technology ramp
  • History of mentoring junior engineers and serving as technical focal point
  • Strong ownership mindset with ability to drive initiatives from concept to factory deployment

Why This Role Defines Your Career

  • Innovation Leadership: Drive breakthrough technologies that set industry standards
  • Global Impact: Your work powers devices used by billions worldwide
  • Cutting-Edge Technology: Work with the most advanced semiconductor processes
  • Elite Collaboration: Partner with world-class suppliers and internal experts
  • Career Growth: Lead initiatives that directly impact Intel's strategic roadmap
  • Mission-Critical: Bridge the gap between research breakthroughs and manufacturing reality

The MDCE Advantage

Join Intel's most dynamic organization where innovation meets manufacturing excellence. MDCE offers unparalleled opportunities to shape the future of semiconductor technology while working with the industry's most advanced processes and brightest minds.

Ready to define the next generation of semiconductor manufacturing?

At MDCE, your expertise doesn't just advance technology… it transforms entire industries. Join us in building the foundation for tomorrow's technological breakthroughs

title: Senior Out-of-Order CPU Architect
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As a CPU Architect, you will be at the forefront of Intel's innovation, shaping the future of CPU designs for high-performance computing and low-power products. This role is integral to Intel's mission to deliver cutting-edge solutions that power the world's technology, from advanced data centers to everyday consumer devices. You will play a pivotal role in driving end-to-end CPU architecture specifications, ensuring optimal performance, power efficiency, scalability, and interoperability across hardware and software. Through creative problem-solving and collaboration, you will influence cross-functional roadmaps, define technology targets, and deliver revolutionary CPU architectures that meet diverse market requirements.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and drive end-to-end CPU architecture specifications based on hardware features, requirements, and lifecycle needs.
  • Define CPU targets for performance, power, frequency, area, and feature content to align with market requirements.
  • Explore new approaches and devise novel architectures that deliver optimized CPUs for multiple segments, from high-performance computing to extreme low-power applications.
  • Invent, conceptualize, and specify architectural and microarchitecture features that address future CPU usage and segment needs.
  • Define and document new instructions to support innovative use cases and improve existing ones, enhancing the instruction set architecture (ISA).
  • Develop and execute test plans and infrastructure for new architectures/features, simulate functional models, and analyze test results using advanced statistical techniques.
  • Propose experimental changes and design alternatives to meet constraints for performance, power, area, and timing.
  • Capable of, but not often required to in your role, of directly implementing your microarchitectural specifications in system verilog. If designers require aid in converging timing and/or power constraints, you are expected to be able to do the work yourself and solve the issues quickly.
  • Review and influence cross-functional roadmaps and collaborate with architects, design, verification, and validation engineers during project execution.
  • Drive definition of new microarchitectures and identify mitigations for issues during feature implementation to improve CPU designs.
  • Expertise in CPU architecture fundamentals, microarchitecture design, low-power design, RTL development, and System Verilog.
  • Proven ability to debug microarchitecture and simulation issues and solve complex design problems.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • 15+ consecutive years of experience within high performance/high frequency ARM or x86 CPU organizations working in either the design or architectural domain. Ideally both.
  • 10+ years of experience working within the out-of-order sections of the CPU pipeline. This includes the areas of wide instruction rename and allocation, uop/instruction schedulers, and execution units.
  • 5+ years writing RTL and owning it through timing and power convergence across multiple generations of a CPU line.
  • 2+ years of experience building deep, high frequency advanced integer and/or floating-point/vector schedulers.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills demonstrated through leadership roles or team management.
  • Effective collaboration skills to work across teams and influence cross-functional roadmaps.
  • Passion for driving innovation and contributing to Intel's mission of delivering world-class technology solutions.


We invite you to join us in shaping the future of computing technology. Apply today to make your mark on the next-generation CPUs driving the world forward.

title: IP RTL Senior Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact:


As an IP Logic Design Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in developing high-quality intellectual property (IP) for Unified Intel Chassis designs. This position is at the forefront of Intel's innovation, ensuring that our products consistently deliver world-class performance, power efficiency, and reliability. Work closely with architects to define and design complex protocol bridges. Define and implement range-based access control for secured memory and register paths across HBW and LBW. Own privilege qualification and policy propagation across AXI-Lite, APB, IOSF-SB, and HBW request paths. Design and validate parity/ECC generation and checking for request, response, and data channels. Define fault behavior for unauthorized accesses and corrupt transactions, including silent block semantics, RAZWI-style handling, poison propagation, and timeout cleanup. Build or integrate logging, interrupt, and firmware-visible error harvesting flows for local and global RAS handling. Support error injection, diagnostics, and post-silicon debug hooks for both security and reliability validation. Define and implement telemetry capture for fabric load, latency, congestion, error context, and other operational health indicators. Own debug and trace data paths for wrapper-level and fabric-level observability, including data capture, transport, formatting, and handoff to downstream debug infrastructure. Design counters, sticky status, snapshots, and firmware-visible CSRs that make performance and failure analysis practical. Integrate trigger, monitor, and logging hooks needed for bring-up, stress triage, and post-silicon correlation. Work with architecture, validation, firmware, and post-silicon teams to ensure telemetry and debug signals are useful, stable, and diagnosable. Balance observability depth against area, timing, bandwidth, and survivability constraints. Support root-cause analysis of bandwidth loss, latency outliers, protocol stalls, and intermittent field or lab issues using hardware observability features.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop logic designs, register transfer level (RTL) coding, and simulations required for IP blocks, functional units, and subsystems.
  • Define architecture and microarchitecture features for the IP block being designed.
  • Apply strategies, tools, and methods to optimize RTL design for power, performance, area, and timing targets.
  • Strong knowledge of AXI, AXI-Lite, APB, parity/ECC schemes, and transaction error handling.

title: Neuromorphic/AI Research Scientist
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel's Neuromorphic Computing Lab has been at the forefront of brain-inspired computing for nearly a decade, working alongside a global ecosystem of 250+ research groups. Our groundbreaking Loihi series research chips have pioneered event-driven, sparse, and massively parallel neuro-inspired processing, resulting in over 100 peer-reviewed publications. As part of Intel's CTO Office, we're now transforming these research breakthroughs into real-world products that will power the next generation of physical AI systems.

We are seeking a Neuromorphic AI Research Scientist to advance state-of-the-art neuromorphic processor technology toward commercial adoption. This role focuses on modeling, prototyping, and defining architectures and algorithms that enable transformative gains for real-world customer applications in edge computing, signal processing, and autonomous systems.

Intel Ireland is a leading centre for semiconductor manufacturing and technology development, producing advanced process technologies that enable Intel products used around the world. title: Staff Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Shape the Future of Semiconductor Innovation at Intel Foundry

Organization Overview

Manufacturing Development Customer Engineering (MDCE) is a newly established organization within Intel Foundry Technology Manufacturing and is focused on accelerating technology ramp and manufacturing excellence. Our mission is to seamlessly transition cutting-edge technologies from development to high-volume production while making technology ramp a key competitive differentiator for Intel Foundry.

Position Summary

MDCE is seeking a Staff Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) Engineer to drive module ownership and technical leadership across Intel's most advanced logic technologies (18A, Intel 3, Intel 12nm). This role requires a seasoned professional who can navigate the complexities of process development, cross-node standardization, and high-volume manufacturing readiness while delivering exceptional results for both Intel products and foundry customers.

Core Responsibilities

Technical Leadership

  • Process Development & Optimization: Lead CMP process development from concept through HVM implementation across multiple advanced technology nodes
  • Cross-Node Alignment: Drive standardization and best practices across Intel's technology portfolio to maximize efficiency and yield
  • Problem Resolution: Own and resolve complex CMP-related yield and manufacturing issues using data-driven approaches and structured problem-solving methodologies

Strategic Execution

  • Customer-Centric Delivery: Align technical strategies with customer requirements and business objectives, ensuring on-time delivery of robust solutions
  • Technology Transfer: Bridge technology development and manufacturing teams to ensure smooth transition of CMP processes to production
  • Continuous Improvement: Drive ongoing optimization initiatives to enhance process capability, yield, and manufacturing efficiency

Collaboration & Leadership

  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Work closely with Integration, Device, Yield, Factory, Quality, and Customer Engineering teams
  • Supplier Engagement: Collaborate with equipment and consumables suppliers to co-develop and optimize CMP solutions
  • Team Development: Mentor junior engineers and provide technical guidance across the organization

Professional Excellence

  • Proven Track Record: History of significant technical accomplishments and successful project delivery
  • Leadership Capability: Ability to influence and drive results across multiple organizations and disciplines
  • Business Acumen: Understanding of semiconductor industry trends, manufacturing strategies, and customer requirements

Personal Attributes

  • Communication Skills: Exceptional ability to communicate complex technical concepts to diverse audiences
  • Adaptability: Thrives in ambiguous situations and can drive clarity in complex technical challenges while work effectively in fast-paced, high-pressure environments
  • Initiative: Self-motivated with strong persistence and ability to work independently
  • Quality Focus: Meticulous attention to detail with commitment to safety, quality, and compliance standards

Qualifications:

The Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position.  Minimum qualifications listed below would be obtained through a combination of industry relevant job experience, internship experience and / or schoolwork/classes/research. The preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, or related technical field
  • 5+ years of experience in semiconductor manufacturing / process development or technology development
  • 3+ years of direct experience in Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) process development experience with hands-on process tuning and characterization
  • Experience with major CMP equipment platforms in one of the following platforms (AMAT, Ebara, etc.)
  • Experience with CMP consumables (e.g. slurries, pads, conditioning disks, filters, clean chemistries)
  • Previous semiconductor foundry experience

Preferred Qualifications

  • Doctorate in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, or related technical field
  • Experience with advanced technology nodes (e.g. sub-10nm logic, specifically in Gate All Around (GAA) architectures with track record of successful technology development and HVM implementation
  • Cross-functional leadership experience, including task force leadership for yield improvement initiatives
  • Experience with CMP integration with other process modules (e.g. deposition, lithography, etch, clean) and CMP-relevant metrology with understanding of CMP impact on device performance and yield.
  • Experience with CMP-relevant metrology and process control (e.g. thickness, topography, defects, roughness, particles)

Work Environment

This role requires in-person collaboration to enable rapid decision-making and effective problem resolution. You'll work in a dynamic, fast-paced environment with competing priorities while maintaining the highest standards for safety, quality, and customer satisfaction.

Impact & Growth

Join a team that's reshaping Intel's foundry capabilities and directly influencing the success of next-generation semiconductor technologies. This role offers exceptional opportunities for professional growth, technical leadership, and meaningful impact on Intel's strategic objectives in the foundry market.

The Role and Impact

As a Strategic/Development Industrial Engineer, you will serve as a driving force behind Intel's manufacturing and capacity planning innovation. In this role, you will analyze complex business data, forecast future capacity needs, and collaborate across teams to design solutions that improve production efficiency, eliminate waste, and reduce costs-all while adhering to technical and quality standards. Your contributions will directly support Intel's ability to deliver cutting-edge technologies to a global market, positioning you to make a tangible impact in shaping Intel's future.

Business group

You will join Intel's Foundry Capacity Optimization (FCO) organization, a team responsible for factory space, capacity, and capital equipment planning. FCO plays a leadership role in defining Intel's growth strategy by enabling data-driven decisions that align with long-term manufacturing objectives, balancing near-term execution with future scalability. As part of this team, you will work collaboratively across Intel's manufacturing, technology development, and finance groups to support the company's broader goals of delivering world-class technology solutions.

  • Develop and execute long-term capacity strategies, considering product roadmaps, architecture, demand variability, factory capabilities, and forecast uncertainties.

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to create detailed execution plans and systems supporting organizational goals.

title: Senior ASIC Verification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Join us to help build the next generation of AI hardware solutions. You will be part of a highly skilled, agile team developing cutting-edge hardware for the AI domain, where we push the boundaries of what silicon can do for emerging AI workloads. With a startup-like culture, we move quickly and give engineers the opportunity to drive significant technical and business impact. We are intentional, fast adopters of AI as a working tool. We bring modern AI assistants and automation into every part of the verification flow — planning, stimulus and checker development, coverage analysis, debug and more — and we

look to our senior verification engineers to help steer that evolution. If you are energized by defining things that have never existed before, value rigorous thinking, and want real scope and short feedback loops - you'll feel right at home here.

This is a senior, hands-on role with broad technical influence. You will own verification for meaningful parts of the chip — complex IPs and subsystems — building the environments that take them to sign-off, with room to influence the methodologies and working flows we adopt as a team.

  • Collaborate closely with architects, designers, DFT, and emulation/bring-up  teams to ensure correctness from block to system level.

  • B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or equivalent.
  • 6+ years of hands-on functional verification experience, with a strong record of taking complex IPs/subsystems to sign-off.

  • Strong intuition for working with AI tools and real interest in using them to advance the verification flow.

title: Security Hardware Integration Engineer
descriptionHtml:

Job Description: 

Join us to help build the next generation of AI hardware solutions. You will be part of a team developing cutting-edge HW for the AI domain, where we push the boundaries of what silicon can do for emerging AI workloads.

We are continuously developing modern and effective working methods, including hands-on adoption of AI tools throughout the chip development flow. The environment is fast-paced and intellectually stimulating. 

Your Mission: Integrate hardware security IP into the SoC/die and define the HW security architecture protecting a large-scale data center's compute, network, and control infrastructure.

title: Senior Photonic-Integrated-Circuit Integration Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The world is transforming - and so is Intel. Intel is a company of bold and curious inventors and problem solvers who create some of the most astounding technological advancements and experiences in the world. With a legacy of relentless innovation and a commitment to bring smart, connected devices to every person on Earth, our diverse and brilliant teams are continually searching for tomorrow's technology and revel in the challenge that changing the world for the better brings. We work every single day to design and manufacture silicon products that empower people's digital lives. Come join us and do something wonderful.

The Role and Impact

As a Silicon Photonics Integrated Circuit Engineer, you will play an instrumental role in defining, designing, and optimizing cutting-edge silicon photonic integrated circuits, including applications in AI datacenter scale-up, laser sources, and pluggable/NPO/CPO/OCI solutions. You will contribute to all stages of chip development, from design and simulation to validation and manufacturing, ensuring high-performance and reliability. Your expertise will directly shape photonic technologies that drive Intel's innovation, making a tangible impact on next-generation solutions.

Business Group

This role is part of Intel's Integrated Photonics Solutions (IPS), a group dedicated to pioneering advancements in silicon photonics and integrated circuit technologies. Our team focuses on high-impact research, design, and development to enable transformative solutions that enhance Intel's technological leadership in the industry. By joining us, you will be part of a collaborative environment that empowers innovation and problem-solving.

Key Responsibilities

  • Architect, design, and optimize complex active and passive silicon photonic integrated circuits.
  • Develop and execute plans for chip design, layout, tape out, test, validation, and performance debug.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with foundries, validation teams, manufacturers, and quality/reliability groups.
  • Conduct data analysis, reliability, qualification, and delivery of known-good-die solutions.
  • Design and simulate photonic integrated circuit systems using advanced modeling tools (such as Lumerical Interconnect, ADS).
  • Drive high-volume manufacturing (HVM) enabling flows and ensure seamless integration of photonic technologies.
  • Develop technical documentation and test content to support the silicon photonics chip lifecycle.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience listed below would be obtained through a combination of your degree, research and or relevant previous job and or internship experiences.

Minimum Qualifications:

Master's degree in relevant fields and 8+ years of industry experience OR a PhD with 6+ years of industry experience.

Required Skills:

  • Experience in development of photonic-integrated-circuits from concept to high volume manufacturing (HVM).
  • Experience designing, simulating, and testing complex PIC's, including link budget analysis, electrical power budgets, back-reflection budgets, Monte Carlo models and other performance indicators. 
  • Familiarity using optical design and simulation tools such as Lumerical (FDTD, MODE, DEVICE, Interconnect), RSoft, Tidy3D, Harold, Photon Design, or numerical simulation tools such as Matlab or Python.
  • Experience contributing to or leading PIC tape-outs.
  • Familiarity with layout tools such as Candence, KLayout, Synopsys Optocompiler, or GDSFactory.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Proven ability to solve problems in group settings and deliver innovative solutions.
  • A track record of driving impactful results in large-scale integrated circuit development.
  • Exposure to standard photonic test methodologies and equipment such as optical spectrum analyzers, tunable lasers, optical backscatter reflectometers, optical vector analyzers, fiber or free-space coupling.
  • Exposure to EDA/PDA tools and methodologies.
  • Familiarity with LVS, SDL, and DRC.
  • PIC test data analysis and design optimization including using statistical analysis using tools such as JMP or statistical libraries in matlab or python. 


If you are passionate about advancing cutting-edge photonic technologies and ready to make a significant impact, we invite you to bring your expertise and creativity to Intel. Join us to shape the future of silicon photonics and redefine what's possible in technology.

title: Semiconductor Device Modeling Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Team

The Compact Device Modeling Group (CDMG) is part of Intel's Design Enablement (DE) organization. DE is a key pillar in enabling Intel to deliver design, development, and manufacturing services that allow internal and external customers to bring winning products to the marketplace. Your work will directly enable design teams to get to market faster with leadership products based on innovative technologies.

As a member of CDMG, you will be at the forefront of co-optimizing Intel's state-of-the-art process technology, enabling customers with diverse design needs to deliver best-in-class products for data-centric applications.

As a Semiconductor Device Modeling Engineer, you will be responsible for characterizing device behavior and generating/updating device models for new technologies while ensuring robust and accurate model simulations.

Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Master's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related discipline with a minimum of 3+ years of industry experience in the semiconductor field; OR
  • PhD in Electrical Engineering or a related discipline with a minimum of 1 year of industry or research experience and a dissertation focused on semiconductor devices or processes.
  • Hands-on experience in Python or C, Shell programming.
  • Experience or course work in semiconductor device physics, process flow, layout and simple circuit design and simulation.
  • The ability to work independently after the initial ramp-up time.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • A Ph.D. degree in electrical engineering or related discipline with 3 + years of industry experience in the semiconductor field.

title: SoC Verification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Team:

You will be joining Intel's cutting-edge product development group, a team focused on designing and verifying advanced semiconductor solutions. This group is at the forefront of innovation, delivering high-quality, scalable products that drive Intel's leadership in technology and performance. By contributing your skills here, you will help shape the future of computing and enable groundbreaking advancements in the industry.

As a SoC Design Verification Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring that Intel's complex System-on-Chip (SoC) designs meet functional specifications and deliver high-quality performance.   • Document and maintain test plans, driving technical reviews with design and architecture teams

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The world is transforming - and so is Intel. Intel is a company of bold and curious inventors and problem solvers who create some of the most astounding technology advancements and experiences in the world. descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Group 

Intel Foundry Quality, Reliability and Labs is focused on strengthening Intel Foundry’s long-term business success through quality, reliability, prevention systems, labs, and customer quality across wafer fabrication, advanced packaging, substrates, assembly, and test. The organization partners across manufacturing, technology development, automation, sourcing, engineering, labs, suppliers, and customer quality to reduce supplier-related risk, improve prevention, and drive sustained quality improvement. 

About the Role 

Intel Foundry is seeking a strategic, results-oriented Senior Director to lead Supplier Quality and Reliability. Reporting to the VP/GM of Intel Foundry Quality, Reliability and Labs, this leader will define the vision and execute the strategy to eliminate supplier-related quality incidents across wafer fabrication, advanced packaging, substrates, assembly, and test. 

This leader will partner with high-impact Intel Foundry leaders across manufacturing, technology development, automation, sourcing, engineering, labs, customer quality, and suppliers to strengthen prevention, accountability, decision-making, and sustained improvement. The ideal candidate brings executive presence, supplier influence, and a record of improving quality across complex global supply chains. External foundry or semiconductor supplier quality leadership experience is preferred.

This role requires periodic domestic and international travel. 

Responsibilities: 

  • Define and execute supplier quality and reliability strategy aligned with Intel Foundry roadmaps and customer commitments. 
  • Lead a global Supplier Quality and Reliability organization across equipment, materials, packaging, assembly, and test. 
  • Communicate supplier performance, risks, decisions, and mitigation plans to executives. 
  • Deploy qualification, audit, surveillance, release, and prevention systems across suppliers and sub-tier suppliers. 
  • Control supplier changes across materials, configurations, firmware/software, packaging, handling, and logistics. 
  • Partner across manufacturing, sourcing, engineering, labs, customer quality, and suppliers to align priorities and reduce risk. 
  • Define metrology and monitoring systems for equipment, incoming materials, and manufacturing process interactions. 
  • Drive containment, root cause, corrective action, recurrence prevention, and supplier accountability for major excursions. 
  • Direct engagement with supplier executives on a peer-to-peer basis for roadmap development and implementation and issue containment and resolution

Experience Required: 

  • Experience with semiconductor quality management systems, supplier qualification, audits, change control, corrective action, and risk reduction. 
  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and drive cross-functional alignment in complex technical environments. 
  • Leadership experience in supplier quality, reliability, manufacturing quality, or supply chain quality within semiconductor, foundry, advanced packaging, or high-tech manufacturing environments. 
  • Experience leading global teams, executive supplier engagements, and quality improvement programs across multi-tier supplier ecosystems. 
  • Strong business acumen with experience connecting technical execution to customer, financial, and operational outcomes. 

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Science, Business, or a related field required. Advanced degree such as an MBA, MS, or PhD preferred.

Job Description: 

About the Group

Intel Foundry Services is Intel's dedicated foundry organization, providing world-class semiconductor manufacturing, advanced packaging, and systems foundry capabilities to external customers. Foundry Services plays a central role in Intel's strategy to deliver leading-edge process technology, manufacturing excellence, and ecosystem partnerships to fabless and integrated device manufacturers worldwide. Intel Foundry Services is looking for a highly collaborative, influential and experienced applicant searching for a high-impact position that bridges business development, competitive intelligence, technology roadmapping, and customer engagement to drive foundry revenue growth and market positioning. title: Platform Power Thermal Performance Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

We are looking for motivated graduate candidates who are interested in platform performance engineering for AI server platforms. In this role, you will learn and contribute to GPU-as-an-I/O-device performance validation and optimization, working across CPU host architecture, I/O subsystems, GPU device interactions, and server-level performance analysis. You will work with experienced engineers to develop validation methodologies, execute performance experiments, analyze results, and support technical issue investigation across reference designs and customer-oriented systems. This role provides a strong opportunity to build hands-on expertise in modern AI infrastructure, from single-server performance tuning to cluster-scale design concepts. Roles and Responsibilities • Learn and contribute to topology validation and performance analysis for AI server platforms, covering CPU host, GPU, memory, storage, and network interactions. • Support validation plan development, benchmark execution, data collection, and result analysis for CPU host and GPU I/O performance studies. • Work with senior engineers to debug performance issues, summarize findings, and propose practical improvement ideas from the host platform perspective. • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to communicate test progress, document technical observations, and support issue closure under guidance.

Qualifications:

This role is designed for graduate candidates who want to grow into platform performance engineers. You will have opportunities to develop practical expertise in AI server architecture, CPU host performance, GPU I/O behavior, benchmarking methodology, and at-scale platform optimization concepts. We value strong technical fundamentals, curiosity, hands-on learning ability, and clear communication. 1. Solid fundamentals in computer architecture, operating systems, or computer systems, with interest in CPU, memory, and I/O subsystem behavior. 2. Basic understanding of GPU computing, parallel programming, or accelerator-based systems; related coursework, research, or project experience is a plus. 3. Interest in AI infrastructure and at-scale system concepts, including server architecture, scale-up/scale-out design, networking, and storage. Candidates should be upcoming graduates with a Master of Science degree, or higher, in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field. The ideal candidate is passionate about learning new technologies, solving complex system problems, and improving validation efficiency through structured analysis and automation. • Solid understanding of computer architecture and system fundamentals; exposure to concepts such as PCIe/CXL, coherency, IOMMU, NUMA, or host-device data movement is a plus. • Basic knowledge of GPU architecture, GPU programming, or AI accelerator software stacks; experience with CUDA, ROCm, OpenCL, SYCL, or related frameworks is a plus. • Interest in AI server and cluster-level system design, including GPU scale-up, server scale-out, networking, storage, and performance bottleneck analysis. • Familiarity with benchmark methodology, performance metrics, and experiment design; hands-on lab, coursework, internship, or research project experience is preferred. • Good programming and scripting skills, such as Python, C/C++, or shell scripting, with the ability to automate tests, process data, and support performance analysis. • Experience in system validation, performance testing, Linux-based development, machine learning/deep learning workloads, networking, storage, or GPU computing through internship, research, or academic projects is a plus. • Strong learning agility, problem-solving mindset, teamwork, and ability to work in a fast-changing technical environment. • Good verbal and written English communication skills, with the ability to document technical findings clearly.

title: Ocotillo Technology Fabrication Defect Metrology Equipment Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel is shaping the future of technology to help create a better future for the entire world. Our work in pushing forward fields like AI, analytics, and cloud-to-edge technology is at the heart of countless innovations. With a career at Intel, you'll have the opportunity to use technology to power major breakthroughs and create enhancements that improve our everyday quality of life. Join us and help make the future more wonderful for everyone. Want to learn more? Visit our YouTube Channel or the link below.

Life at Intel


Intel is looking for highly motivated individuals with strong technical background and capabilities to sustain, ramp, and transfer all technology nodes in Arizona. They will drive rapid continuous improvements in safety, quality, yield, reliability, cost, process stability/capability, and productivity while maintaining rigorous quality control.


Intel Foundry is increasing its investment in defect metrology technology, implementing a new Win It Inline initiative using advanced real-time monitoring to improve yield learning cycles. Investing in inline metrology will give engineers more data throughout the manufacturing process, as opposed to waiting for end of the line data - a fundamental shift in how we leverage data to build chips.
Role Overview: As a Defect Metrology Equipment Engineer, you will play a critical role in optimizing and maintaining metrology systems for manufacturing. You will collaborate closely with equipment development, operations, automation, and manufacturing teams to enhance yield systems and ensure product integrity.


Responsibilities will include but are not limited to:
- Perform statistical analysis and develop visualizations to construct accurate process development roadmaps.
- Develop methods and systems to analyze diverse big data sources, leading to yield modeling and process roadmap definition.
- Develop and maintain systems that enable faster interpretation of fab process, defect, and electrical data to drive process changes for yield enhancement.
- Transform experimental and manufacturing data into yield improvement actions.
- Ensure manufacturability over process and product design through thorough analysis.
- Execute new product introductions and participate in design of experiments.
- Develop tools and algorithms for high-volume data analysis to identify yield limiters.
- Harden equipment systems to meet operational needs for leading-edge logic nodes.
- Develop AI/ML applications to improve patterning solutions and design efficiency.
- Collaborate with internal teams to ensure data integrity and implement custom algorithms.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.


Experience listed below would be obtained through a combination of your school work/classes/research and/or relevant previous job and/or internship experiences.

Minimum Qualifications:
• 3+ months experience with Yield and Defect Metrology equipment (e.g. KLA, AMAT, ASML HMI, TEL, Keysight, Advantest, and Hitachi).

• Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Microelectronics Engineering, Material Science Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Optical Engineering, Statistics/Data Science, Chemistry, Physics, or related field of study AND 2+ years relevant experience OR
• Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Microelectronics Engineering, Material Science Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Optical Engineering, Statistics/Data Science, Chemistry, Physics, or related field of study AND 1+ years relevant experience.



Preferred Qualifications:

•Advanced degree and 2+ years of applications experience with defect metrology tools.
• Knowledge of Semiconductor fabrication and processing techniques (Lithography, Etch, CMP, Thin Films, Plating, etc.), Statistical Process Control and Design of experiments (DOE) principles, Statistical Data Analysis. (Examples include: JMP/JSL, Python, SQL) and/or Programing Experience in JMP/JSL, Python, R and SQL.
• Experience in Laser Optics, Scanning Electron Microscopy, Digital Signal Processing, and Image Processing.
• Experience in technical documentation, training, and project management.
• 3+ years of New Technology startup experience.
• 3+ years of relevant experience in Process/Yield Engineering.
• Demonstrate strong technical and troubleshooting skills.
• Experience in manufacturing environment.
• Experience in metrology.
• Demonstrate exceptional customer orientation.
• Demonstrate the ability to work across organizational boundaries including process engineering, integration and yield.
• Good communication skills with a high tolerance to ambiguous and changing situations

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact

As a Module Equipment Technician, you will play a critical role in Intel's high-tech manufacturing process, ensuring our tools are optimized for world-class production. Your contributions will directly impact Intel's innovation, enabling the delivery of advanced technologies that power the future of computing. This is an exciting opportunity to grow your technical expertise, work alongside engineering teams, and be part of a collaborative environment where your skills make a tangible difference.

This role has openings available in all functional areas, Litho, Wet Etch, Dry Etch, Diffusion, Implant, Planar and Thin Films. This role has opportunities across all shifts (4/5/6/7) as needed per functional area.

title: Silicon Photonics Component Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

As a Silicon Photonics (SiPho) Component Design Engineer, you will join Intel Foundry's Silicon Photonics Process Development and Manufacturing (SPDM) team, which is driving process innovation and enabling the next generation of optical interconnect technologies. Since pioneering the world's first heterogeneous silicon laser nearly a decade ago, Intel has continued to lead the industry through advanced technology development and scalable high-volume manufacturing.

Our team is committed to expanding Intel Foundry's Silicon Photonics platform to support customer solutions across data center communications, co-packaged optics, and next-generation optical networking technologies ranging from 400G to 3.2T+ and beyond.

In this role, you will contribute to the development and optimization of silicon photonic components that power cutting-edge optical communication systems. You will collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering teams to design, characterize, and improve photonic devices while advancing Intel Foundry's silicon photonics technology roadmap.

Key Responsibilities

Photonic Component Design and Development

  • Design, simulate, and support the development of photonic components, including lasers, modulators, high-speed photodetectors, passive devices, and waveguide structures.
  • Contribute to photonic integrated circuit (PIC) design and architecture evaluations.

Device Optimization and Analysis

  • Perform simulations, tolerance studies, and design evaluations to improve device performance, manufacturability, and reliability.
  • Apply established modeling methodologies and design best practices to optimize photonic components.

Test Chip Development and Validation

  • Support test chip execution activities, including design implementation, layout coordination, tape-out preparation, and silicon validation.
  • Collaborate with fabrication and test teams to ensure successful design realization.

Characterization and Data Analysis

  • Analyze characterization and test data to identify performance trends, root causes, and opportunities for design enhancement.
  • Support the implementation of design improvements based on experimental results.

Modeling and Methodology Development

  • Contribute to photonic device models, simulation workflows, and automation tools.
  • Drive improvements in test methodologies and engineering processes to increase development efficiency.

Research and Technology Innovation

  • Evaluate emerging photonic technologies and support proof-of-concept demonstrations.
  • Contribute to intellectual property development through patents, technical publications, and innovation activities.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

  • PhD in Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related technical discipline with 2+ years of experience in silicon photonic device design, simulation, characterization, or related research environments;

or

  • Master's degree in a related field with 4+ years of relevant experience.
  • Experience in one or more of the following areas:
    • High-speed photonic devices, including optical modulators and photodetectors;
    • Photonic design and simulation using tools such as Sentaurus, Silvaco, Lumerical, HFSS, ADS, RSoft, or equivalent;
    • Photonic device testing and characterization; data analysis using MATLAB, Python, JMP, or similar tools;
    • Photonic layout design using Cadence, KLayout, or comparable design environments.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to work effectively in a collaborative, cross-functional engineering environment.
  • Experience with silicon photonic modulator or detector design.
  • Familiarity with micro-ring modulators or advanced photonic materials such as BTO, TFLN, or III-V integration.
  • Basic understanding of high-speed electronic ICs including TIAs, drivers, equalization techniques, and DSP concepts.
  • Experience with optical link modeling and system-level performance analysis.
  • Experience with photonic devices operating at 100G+ data rates.
  • Familiarity with semiconductor foundry development processes.
  • Publications, conference presentations, or patent contributions in photonics or related fields.
  • Experience working on customer-facing, product development, or cross-functional engineering projects.
  • Experience with active and passive silicon photonic devices including heaters, carrier injection devices, and passive waveguide structures.

title: AI GPU Cache Designer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact As a SoC Cache Design Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in developing cutting-edge Cache subsystem design for Intel's AI SoCs. You will drive the micro architecture, register transfer level (RTL) coding, subsystem integration, and simulation processes to deliver high-quality, fully verified Cache that meet power, performance, and area targets. Your work will directly contribute to Intel's groundbreaking AI hardware solutions, ensuring they meet the rigorous demands of modern applications. Business group Intel's AI SoC organization is at the forefront of developing innovative products that power AI applications across diverse domains. From edge devices to data center accelerators, our team focuses on delivering high-performance, efficient, and scalable hardware solutions. As part of this group, you will collaborate with world-class engineers to advance Intel's leadership in AI hardware development and help shape the future of intelligent computing. Key Responsibilities - Evaluate architectural trade-offs to align design features with performance targets, power constraints, and system limitations. - Define and document microarchitecture specifications for complex SoC IP blocks, implement RTL in Verilog/SystemVerilog, and deliver synthesis- and timing-clean designs. - Collaborate closely with verification teams to ensure comprehensive validation and coverage of all design aspects. - Develop and maintain timing constraints for IP blocks, supporting physical design teams in synthesis, timing closure, and formal equivalence checks. - Lead silicon bring-up efforts, including post-silicon validation, debug, and performance analysis. - Mentor junior engineers and contribute to advancing best practices for design methodology and quality assurance.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications - Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field, with 12+ years of experience in RTL design for ASIC/SoC development; OR Master's degree in relevant field with 8+ years of experience; OR PhD in relevant field with 6+ years of experience. - Advanced proficiency in RTL design using Verilog/SystemVerilog and hands-on experience in SoC system integration. - Expertise in standard bus protocols (AXI, AHB) and embedded processor architectures. - Demonstrated ability to address design challenges, including clock domain crossings, power optimization, and timing closure. - Proficiency in scripting languages (e.g., Python, TCL) for automation and design flow customization. Preferred Qualifications - Strong knowledge of high-speed and low-power design techniques. - Familiarity with industry-standard EDA tools such as HDL simulators (VCS, Questa, IES), lint tools (Spyglass), and FPGA prototyping tools (Xilinx Vivado, Altera Quartus II). - Experience in SoC multicore CPU subsystem design and GPU cache development. - Collaborative mindset and leadership skills, with a passion for innovation and solving complex technical challenges. Join us to shape the next generation of AI hardware and make an impact on tomorrow's technological advancements.

title: Senior GPU Performance Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role

The Software and AI (SAI) organization is seeking a highly skilled software engineer to contribute to the development and low-level optimization of oneDNN, a complex, cross-platform, open-source performance library that serves as the foundation for deep learning applications (github.com/uxlfoundation/oneDNN).Please Note: This is a low-level software engineering and hardware-acceleration role. It does not involve building, training, or tuning machine learning models. Instead, you will focus on developing highly optimized math primitives, parallel algorithms, and GPU kernels that power industry-leading AI frameworks (such as OpenVINO, TensorFlow, PyTorch, and ONNX Runtime) on Intel hardware.

Key Responsibilities

Kernel Development and Architecture
  • Develop high-performance GEMM, convolution, and attention kernels for AI workloads
  • Design scalable JIT and codegen infrastructure for GPU kernel generation
Low-Level Optimization
  • Implement fusion and memory-traffic optimizations to maximize hardware utilization
  • Optimize mixed-precision and quantized execution paths (e.g., BF16, FP16, INT8, FP8, FP4, etc.)
Performance Modeling and Profiling
  • Build analytical and empirical performance models for kernel dispatch and tuning
  • Profile and eliminate performance bottlenecks across oneDNN GPU primitives and runtime paths
Hardware and Software Co-Design
  • Co-design GPU primitives and kernel architectures for next-generation Intel GPUs
  • Partner with hardware and compiler teams to shape future accelerator capabilities and software stacks
Infrastructure and Validation
  • Improve validation, benchmarking, and CI infrastructure for performance-critical GPU workloads

Why Join Us

Massive Scale
  • Work on a global, high-impact open-source library that scales AI performance across millions of devices worldwide
Cutting-Edge Hardware
  • Get early access to and influence the software stack for Intel's roadmap of next-generation discrete GPUs
Expert Collaboration
  • Work alongside industry-leading experts in GPU compilers, hardware architecture, and performance libraries
Total Rewards
  • Enjoy a competitive package including stock programs, quarterly bonuses, robust healthcare, and highly flexible hybrid/remote working options

What We're Looking For

To be successful in this role, you should demonstrate the following professional traits:
  • A strong ownership mindset — you take initiative on complex, ambiguous technical problems and drive them to resolution
  • A collaborative approach — you work effectively across hardware, compiler, and framework teams to align on shared technical goals
  • A performance-driven curiosity — you are motivated by squeezing every cycle out of hardware and continuously seek deeper understanding of low-level systems

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications
  • Education: BSc, MSc, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, or a highly technical related field
  • Core Language: 5+ years of professional software development experience with expert-level modern C++
  • Performance Optimizations: 2+ years of hands-on experience in programming and kernel optimization on GPUs (via SYCL/DPC++, OpenCL, CUDA, or HIP), or at least 5+ years of similar low-level performance optimization experience on CPUs
  • Hardware Architecture: Strong foundations in computer architecture, cache hierarchies, memory subsystems, and parallel programming paradigms (e.g., multi-threading, SIMD/vectorization)
Preferred Qualifications
  • Math Libraries: Experience developing high-performance math libraries (e.g., GEMM, convolution, reduction, or FFT kernels)
  • Low-Level Tuning: Hands-on experience with GPU assembly-level tuning or compiler optimization
  • Parallel APIs: Familiarity with parallel programming APIs such as OpenMP or oneTBB
  • AI Workload Context: Basic understanding of deep learning primitives (e.g., forward/backward passes) to understand how library code is utilized by upstream frameworks

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact  
As a Facilities Instrumentation and Controls Engineer, you will design, develop, and maintain industrial instrumentation and automation systems essential for supporting facilities operations, manufacturing, labs and other stakeholders. Your role will involve troubleshooting and optimizing existing systems while also creating new control solutions to improve performance and reliability. Your scope also focuses on Building Monitoring System (BMS), PLCs, Control Valves and Monitoring sensors. By playing a key role in ensuring seamless functionality of critical systems, you will directly contribute to enhancing operational efficiency and maintaining Intel's high standards of performance and innovation. 
 
Business group  
The Facilities Engineering team focuses on delivering robust engineering solutions that support Intel's manufacturing and facilities infrastructure. This group is dedicated to maintaining and optimizing systems that ensure operational excellence, reliability, and sustainability across Intel's facilities. The team collaborates across disciplines to support Intel's broader mission of driving innovation and advancing technological capabilities. 
 
Key Responsibilities  
- Design, develop, and maintain industrial instrumentation systems for facilities operations.  
- Troubleshoot, calibrate, and program analytical instrumentation to ensure optimal performance and functionality.  
- Develop and modify control systems to enhance system reliability and efficiency.  
- Conduct root cause failure analysis and implement solutions to address and rectify issues.  
- Prepare engineering assessments and provide technical direction for construction designs.  
- Manage projects within defined cost and time constraints, ensuring adherence to health and safety regulations and quality standards.  
- Collaborate with cross-disciplinary teams, including design engineers, operations staff, and external contractors.

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Electronics, Mechatronics Engineering, or a related field with 2-5 years of hands-on experience in instrumentation and controls

- Experience with industrial automation platforms, such as GE Cimplicity, Rockwell Automation Logix PLC products, and SCADA systems, is highly valued and will be added advantage.  
- Ability to interpret instrumentation installation drawings, PLC Logic diagrams, and interface systems for PLC/SCADA.  
 
Preferred Qualifications

title: Module Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

This is a central requisition for all Ocotillo Technology Fabrication (OTF) functional areas. Successful candidates will be aligned to the areas that match best with factory needs.

Join Intel and build a better tomorrow. Intel is in the midst of an exciting transformation, with a vision to create and extend computing technology to connect and enrich the lives of every person on Earth. Our high-volume manufacturing facility in Chandler, Arizona is looking for amazing talent. Join and help us create the next generation of technologies that will shape the future for decades to come.

The Ocotillo Technology Fabrication (OTF) Module Engineer role is multifaceted. The ideal candidate will have a passion for instrumentation and equipment with the goal of developing a robust manufacturable process module.
This is a central requisition for all functional areas: Litho, Wet Etch, Dry Etch,  Diffusion, Implant, Planar and Thin Films. Successful candidates will be aligned to the areas that match best with factory needs.

As an OTF Module Engineer you will play an important role in the OTF engineering team. You will be responsible for owning all aspects of one or more of the factory's 300mm toolsets. Your sustaining responsibilities will include the safety and cleanliness of your area and ensuring Copy Exactly for your toolset. You will also be expected to review the relevant control charts and tool output daily and ensure your toolset and layers remain excursion free. You will be responsible for delivering Model of Record (MOR) availability and achieving 100 percent matching for all relevant operations. For new technology start-ups, you will be responsible for tool installations, conversions, and qualifications; and sustained matching performance. You will be expected to drive continuous improvement in the health and matching of your toolset(s) by maintaining and driving an improvement roadmap. You will be responsible for leading your tools and area to achieve record tool availability, cycle time, and record low defect densities in support of OTFs factory goals. OTF supports a High-Volume Manufacturing. As such, your role may include elements of module-level process development in support of the factory's goal and output.

Responsibilities will include but are not limited to:
o Define roadmaps to meet requirements, goals and milestones for a new technology process.
o Defines and establishes flow, procedures, and equipment configuration for the module.
o Selects and develops material and equipment for the process to meet quality, yield, reliability, cost, productivity and manufacturability requirements.
o Plans and conducts experiments to fully characterize the process throughout the development cycle.
o Drives improvements on quality, yield, reliability, process stability, productivity and safety/ergonomic over variables such as material, method, equipment, environment and operating personnel.
o Develop solutions to problems utilizing formal education, statistical knowledge, and problem-solving tools.
o Establishes process control systems for the process module and sustains the module through volume ramp.
o Develops strategy to resolve difficult problems and establishes systems to deal with these problems in the future.
o Trains production/receiving process engineers for transfer to other factories.
o Transfers process to high volume manufacturing and provide support in new factory start-up as well as install and qualification of the new production lines.
o Position may require working on a day or night shift as an OSE (on-shift engineer) to support toolset needs.

In addition to the qualifications a successful candidate will demonstrate:
o Working in a high performing team culture which includes setting high expectations.
o Driving accountability to those expectations with a high sense of urgency.
o Role modeling the desired culture.
o Possess teamwork and leadership skills.
o Problem solving and prioritization skills.
o Driving high performance maintenance goals for the group.
o Use data to influence factory and virtual factory direction.
o Listening, written and verbal communication.
o Deal with ambiguity in defining activities and direction.
o Commitment to tasks.
o Work across organizational boundaries including process engineering, integration and yield.

What we offer:

We give you opportunities to transform technology and create a better future, by delivering products that touch the lives of every person on earth. As a global leader in innovation and new technology, we foster a collaborative, supportive, and exciting environment where the brightest minds in the world come together to achieve exceptional results. We offer a competitive salary and financial benefits such as bonuses, life and disability insurance, and opportunities to buy Intel stock at a discounted rate. We provide benefits that promote a healthy, enjoyable life: excellent medical plans, wellness programs, and amenities, time off, recreational activities, discounts on various products and services, and much more creative perks that make Intel a Great Place to Work. We're constantly working on making a more connected and intelligent future, and we need your help. Change tomorrow. Start today.

Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Minimum Qualifications:

- Bachelor's degree with 8+ years of experience OR Master’s degree with 6+ years of experience, OR PhD degree with 2+ years of experience in Electrical Engineering, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical or related engineering STEM field.

The experience mentioned above should be in the following:

  • Engineering experience in the semiconductor industry.
  • Experience supporting high-volume manufacturing ramps and technology transfers.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Engineering experience in advanced node semiconductor foundry.
  • Experience working in a semiconductor factory as a technician or engineer prior to Engineering role.
  • Statistics and experimental design; and the skills to apply that knowledge to tool matching, tool qualification, and process development.

title: Tool Equipment Install Engineer (Contract)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Join Intel Foundry Construction and Sourcing (FCS), a team dedicated to building and optimizing world-class semiconductor manufacturing facilities. FCS drives the construction and tool installation of cutting-edge factories that power Intel's global operations. As part of this group, you'll contribute to groundbreaking projects that shape the future of technology and innovation.

 As a key member of the Project Execution Team, the Tool Equipment Install Engineer is an individual contributor reporting to the Tool Install Manager. A key to this role will be close engagement with customers, stakeholders, and partners as well as leadership of the site project execution team.

 This is an onsite position in Phoenix, Arizona. This role will require supporting teams to solve site Tool Install Qual constraints, Scheduling Issues, and participating in Task Forces when required. It will require regular on-site engagement with stakeholders as well as virtually working with others across sites.

 The primary responsibilities for this role will include, but are not limited to: 

  • Collaborate with Factory owners / stakeholders to ensure Tools/Equipment/Kits are ordered and delivered in alignment with the Tool Install schedule requirements, tracking and resolving any issues timely and escalating as required.
  • Represent local FCS site in Central Tool Install and Virtual Factory forums.
  • Work with Stakeholders to Forecast Equipment workload and funding requirements and ensure alignment with FCS Financial Planning/Reporting Cycles.
  • Ensure commit / PO's are in place for Tools/Equipment/Kits to meet the program goals.
  • Collaborate with EMS and Systems Owners ensuring Systems correctly reflect Equipment requirements and schedule.
  • Drive Systems and Part number configuration/genealogy and accuracy for RFT (right first time) Order / Kits delivery.
  • Align all stakeholders to enable detailed execution planning to support Tool Install Milestones / activities.
  • Lead meetings for Planning and Co-ordination across multiple suppliers, trade contractors, and other project stakeholders.
  • Work with Suppliers to ensure business needs are understood and that Equipment, Materials and Resources are positioned to deliver services on time.
  • Maintain awareness of any commercial issues / risks / capacity with Contractors to enable early course correction / resolution.
  • Ensure all stakeholders are trained, competent and comply with SOP's/Procedures.
  • Request and process timely funding requests before work commences to prevent ATFCO's. (After the fact Change Orders)
  • Review and provide feedback, incorporate cross-site learnings into Tool Install operations.
  • Ensure scope is carried out in a manner that meets Intel safety, protocol/housekeeping and quality standards and expectations
  • Translate business and technical requirements into high-quality project plans that enable accurate and cost-effective delivery of scope.
  • Foster innovation and transform traditional tool construction and commissioning practices by driving new methods and solutions through leveraging industry insights.
  • Build and drive safety culture of caring in every business environment, office to the construction sites, and from front-end planning to construction execution.
  • Escalate constraints where necessary and assist in the timely removal of roadblocks.
  • Act as the primary Intel equipment owner from pre-design through SL2 Signoff in mitigating install and facility problems, who is expected to drive troubleshooting efforts to lean, decisive resolution in order to mitigate delays on assigned projects.

A successful candidate will have proven experience demonstrating the following skills and behavioral traits:

  • Manage discussions with executive management, drilling down to details and managing efforts hands-on if the need arises.
  • Leadership, communication, and planning skills.
  • Champion the safety culture of caring onsite throughout execution of assigned scope.
  • Drive decision making, integrating with business partners, and influencing in a highly matrix environment.
  • Ability to identify improvements, develop concepts, problem solving.
  • Skills to drive decision making and change at the cadence Moore's law required.
  • Effective communication and teamwork skills to drive results in a fast-paced environment.

 This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.

Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position.

  • Master's degree in Engineering, Architecture or related technical field with no prior professional experience.

Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. 

  • Familiarity with advanced semiconductor fabrication processes and equipment installation requirements.

  • Proven problem-solving skills, including root cause analysis and technical validation.
  • Proficiency in configuration management, equipment troubleshooting, and manufacturing process control.
  • Strong understanding of environmental health and safety (EHS) guidelines related to tool installation and operation.
  • Ability to interpret technical documentation and apply disciplined execution in project management tasks.
