title: Manufacturing Systems Engineer in Wafer Packaging Manufacturing
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

This role requires regular onsite presence to support the successful development, ramp, and ongoing operation of a high-volume manufacturing or technology development fabrication facility. The position provides both tactical and strategic operational support, leveraging technical expertise to enable new product introductions (NPI), optimize factory performance, and sustain manufacturing operations.

Key Responsibilities

Manufacturing Operations & Process Improvement

  • Support new product introduction (NPI) builds and sustain manufacturing processes throughout the product lifecycle.
  • Define manufacturing requirements, evaluate manufacturing technologies, and develop manufacturing and supply chain plans to support production goals.
  • Analyze and improve existing manufacturing processes, identifying opportunities for optimization and correcting process deviations.
  • Inspect and assess machinery, equipment, and tooling performance, initiating corrective actions for identified issues.
  • Analyze key factory metrics and drive initiatives that improve overall operational performance, capacity, and factory health.

Data Analytics & Decision Support

  • Develop and implement manufacturing decision-support tools, methodologies, and operational standards.
  • Analyze data to identify system enhancements and optimization opportunities and drive implementation roadmaps.
  • Develop, enhance, and troubleshoot factory reporting systems to provide actionable operational insights.
  • Partner with automation teams to create business systems and processes that monitor and improve factory performance.

Stakeholder Collaboration & Operational Support

  • Collaborate with factory operations management, engineering, automation teams, and supply chain partners to align manufacturing strategies with operational goals.
  • Support Manufacturing Operations Managers and their teams in achieving output and performance objectives.
  • Work cross-functionally to resolve issues affecting factory operations, capacity, productivity, and overall manufacturing effectiveness.
  • Provide guidance to product, module, and supply chain engineering teams throughout equipment selection, design, qualification, and implementation.

Manufacturing Systems & Documentation

  • Develop and maintain manufacturing documentation supporting product design, configuration, process requirements, and build execution.
  • Define and drive requirements for automation station controllers and manufacturing systems supporting key product roadmaps.
  • Own and manage factory support equipment, including:
    • Command center workstations
    • Factory laptops
    • Small form factor manufacturing devices and compute elements (e.g., Intel NUCs)
    • Associated factory support equipment and infrastructure

Impact

This role serves as a critical link between manufacturing operations, engineering, automation, and supply chain organizations, ensuring efficient factory execution, continuous improvement, and scalable manufacturing solutions that support current and future product roadmaps.

Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

Minimum Qualifications 

Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Operations Research, or a related engineering discipline, with at least 2 years of relevant professional experience; or a Master’s degree in one of these fields, with at least 1 year of relevant professional experience.

Experience listed above should be a combination of the following:

  • Experience in semiconductor manufacturing, foundry operations, industrial engineering, or operations research within a high-volume production environment.
  • Data analytics and/or programming tools including SQL, Python, Microsoft Excel, JMP, and/or C#.

This position is not eligible for Intel Immigration sponsorship.

Preferred Qualifications

- Knowledge of operations research principles including factory physics and optimization techniques such as linear programming, mixed-integer programming, or constraint-based modeling, with a demonstrated ability to apply these concepts to solve complex manufacturing challenges.
- Experience working cross-functionally with operations, Industrial Engineering, production planning, and supply chain stakeholders in a high-volume manufacturing setting.
- Demonstrated ability to solve complex multi-product optimization problems, analyze factory data, identify root causes using model-based problem solving, and drive corrective actions that improve output, cycle time, and operational efficiency in a manufacturing environment.
- 5+ years of experience in semiconductor foundry operations, high-volume fab manufacturing, industrial engineering, or operations research applied to wafer fabrication, advanced packaging, or production engineering environments.

- Expertise in optimization and simulation techniques, including the development and validation of linear optimization models, mixed-integer programming, and discrete-event simulation tools applied to production scheduling, capacity planning, and factory flow optimization.
- Experience with advanced data extraction, analysis, and programming tools such as Python, SQL, C#, or C++, with the ability to develop and maintain decision-support applications, factory dashboards, and automated reporting systems that provide real-time visibility into factory health and performance metrics.
- Strong communication and leadership skills with the ability to translate complex manufacturing and optimization challenges into clear operational actions, manage customer-facing delivery commitments, and influence cross-functional teams including Finance, Industrial Engineering, Global Supply Management, Process Engineering, and Automation at all levels of the organization.

title: System and Hardware Enabling Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel Edge Computing Engineering Team is on a mission to enable successful ODMs and customers in India to develop differentiated Edge products based on Intel technologies. 


The team is looking for an experienced Digital Design Engineer with strong board-level hardware design, design-review, hardware-enabling and debug expertise to support customers developing platforms based on Intel Core and Atom processors. 


The engineer will work closely with customer hardware teams through the complete board design and enabling lifecycle, including schematic design and review, high-speed interface implementation, PCB layout review, prototype board bring-up, hardware debug, root-cause analysis and resolution of design issues. 

The role requires strong hands-on knowledge of processor-based digital hardware design and the ability to independently review and debug complex customer boards.


The engineer will also provide periodic technical training to customers and proactively support customer design-review, board-debug and technical-support requests to help accelerate successful product development.


Key Responsibilities:


1.    Board-Level Digital Design and Review: Support board-level digital hardware design and conduct detailed design reviews for customer products based on Intel Core and Atom processors. 


2.    Schematic Review: Review customer schematics against Intel Platform Design Guides, reference schematics, datasheets, design checklists and other technical collateral, and identify potential design issues before PCB fabrication. 


3.    Digital Interface Design: Review processor interfaces and associated circuitry, including DDR4/DDR5/LPDDR4/LPDDR5 memory; PCIe; USB; SATA; DisplayPort/eDP/HDMI and other display interfaces; Ethernet and connectivity interfaces; I2C/SMBus, SPI, UART and GPIO; and clock, reset, boot/configuration straps and other platform control signals. 


4.    PCB Layout Review: Review multilayer PCB stack-up and board layout implementation for processor-based platforms, including controlled impedance, high-speed routing, length matching, differential-pair routing, reference planes, via structures and signal-return paths for compliance with Intel layout guidelines and industry best practices. 


5.    High-Speed Digital Design: Perform detailed schematic and layout reviews of high-speed digital interfaces, particularly DDR, PCIe and USB, and recommend corrective actions based on Intel design guidelines and sound high-speed digital design practices. 


6.    Component Selection and Implementation: Support selection and design implementation of board-level digital components including memory devices, clock devices, level translators, buffers, multiplexers, switches, retimers, interface controllers and supporting logic. 


7.    Board Bring-Up and Debug: Drive and support customer board bring-up, including initial power-on, processor initialization, boot failures, memory initialization issues, high-speed interface failures and other board-level hardware issues. 


8.    Hands-On Lab Debug: Use lab debug equipment such as oscilloscopes, digital multimeters, logic analyzers, protocol analyzers, I2C/SMBus tools and programmers to isolate and resolve hardware issues. 


9.    Root-Cause Analysis: Analyze hardware debug data to identify root causes, differentiate between schematic, PCB-layout, component, assembly, manufacturing and configuration-related issues, and recommend corrective actions. 


10.  Customer Issue Resolution: Actively support and drive resolution of customer technical issues, design-review requests and board-debug requests on an ongoing and periodic basis, working with customers from problem definition through root-cause identification and closure. 


11.  Customer Technical Training: Develop and deliver periodic technical training sessions and workshops for customer engineering teams covering Intel processor-based board design, hardware design guidelines, high-speed interfaces, schematic/layout best practices, board bring-up and debug methodologies. 

12.  Customer Hardware Enabling: Provide hands-on technical guidance to customer hardware engineers during schematic design, PCB development, prototype bring-up, EVT/DVT and initial product-enabling phases. 


13.  Cross-Functional Issue Resolution: Collaborate with Intel silicon, platform, validation, BIOS/Firmware and other engineering teams when customer hardware issues require cross-functional investigation and resolution. 


14.  Technical Communication: Effectively communicate design-review findings, technical risks, debug results and recommended corrective actions to customer and internal engineering teams. 


15.  Design Best Practices: Develop and maintain hardware design-review checklists, debug procedures, technical training materials, design best practices and lessons learned for reuse across customer programs. 


16. Customer Engagement: Periodically engage with customer engineering teams to review active designs, understand technical issues and provide timely engineering support throughout their product-development lifecycle.  

Qualifications:

Required Qualifications:


  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electronics/Electrical Engineering or a related discipline, with 8 to 12 years of relevant industry experience, preferably including substantial hands-on experience in processor-based board design and debug. 
  • Strong hands-on experience designing and debugging complex multilayer digital boards, preferably using Intel Core/Atom or similar high-performance processor/SoC platforms. 
  • Experience in schematic capture and review using industry-standard EDA tools such as Cadence OrCAD/Allegro, Siemens/Mentor Graphics Xpedition or equivalent. 
  • Strong experience in processor-based schematic design/review, including CPU/SoC interfaces, DDR memory, PCIe, USB, SATA, display interfaces, Ethernet/connectivity, clock/reset, SPI/I2C/SMBus/UART/GPIO, and boot and configuration circuitry. 
  • Strong understanding of high-speed digital board design principles, including controlled impedance, differential signaling, termination, propagation delay, length/skew matching, crosstalk, return-path discontinuities and via effects. 
  • Experience with 8 to 16+ layer PCB designs, PCB stack-ups and placement/routing reviews for complex processor platforms. 
  • Ability to interpret and apply processor datasheets, platform design guides, reference schematics, layout guidelines and hardware design checklists to customer hardware designs. 
  • Strong hands-on experience with board bring-up and hardware failure analysis, particularly processor boot, memory initialization and high-speed interface issues. 
  • Experience using lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, digital multimeters, logic analyzers, protocol analyzers and other board-level debug tools. 
  • Good understanding of PCB fabrication, assembly processes, DFM/DFT considerations and hardware failure mechanisms. 
  • Ability to independently analyze complex board-level problems, perform root-cause analysis and drive technical issues toward corrective action and closure. 
  • Ability to work directly with customers, manage multiple concurrent design-review and debug requests, and provide timely technical support. 
  • Strong technical presentation and communication skills with the ability to conduct technical training and workshops for customer engineering teams. 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Experience designing, reviewing or supporting boards based on Intel Core or Atom processors. 
  • Experience with embedded and Edge compute designs such as COM Express, COM-HPC, 3.5-inch SBC, Mini-ITX, embedded compute modules and custom industrial platforms. 
  • Hands-on experience with DDR4/DDR5/LPDDR memory design, layout review and debug. 
  • Experience reviewing high-speed interfaces such as PCIe Gen4/Gen5, USB 3.x/USB4, DisplayPort and high-speed Ethernet. 
  • Familiarity with industry-standard Signal Integrity analysis/simulation tools from Cadence, Siemens EDA or equivalent, with the ability to understand and interpret simulation results. 
  • Experience working directly with ODM/OEM/customer engineering teams during schematic review, PCB review, prototype board bring-up and technical issue resolution. 
  • Experience developing and delivering technical training, workshops or design-guideline sessions for hardware engineering teams. 
  • Strong customer-facing communication, problem-solving and technical presentation skills. 
  • Willingness to travel to customer locations across India on a need basis for design reviews, technical training, board bring-up and hardware debug support. 


Primary Location: Bangalore, India 


Travel to customer locations across India on a need basis to support hardware design reviews, customer technical training, board bring-up and debug activities.

title: Senior Network Security/AI Software Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Senior Network Security Software Development Engineer will lead the architecture, development, and delivery of open-source, high-performance network security and AI reference solutions for the Network Software Enabling team in the Enterprise/Cloud Networking segment. This role works closely with architects, customers, and ecosystem partners to define technical requirements and to build reference workloads, with best known methods and configurations, optimized for Intel® Xeon® processors and accelerators across on-prem, edge, and cloud deployments.

The successful candidate will drive the design and optimization of security data planes and AI-enabled security workloads. These include Next-Generation Firewall, Secure Web Gateway, SD-WAN etc. focusing on key performance areas such as scale-up, load distribution, crypto processing, pattern matching, and the migration to AI-driven security functions. The role requires expertise in high-performance packet processing, network security functions, hardware acceleration, performance engineering, and deployment automation.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the architecture and technical roadmap for one or more network security reference solutions, and keep design consistent across the portfolio.
  • Design and optimize packet-processing and security pipelines for throughput, latency, and TCO on current and upcoming Intel® Xeon® platforms.
  • Integrate hardware acceleration technologies (QAT, AVX-512/AMX, NIC offloads) into open-source security stacks such as Snort3, VPP, and Hyperscan.
  • Enable and optimize AI/ML models for security use cases such as malicious URL detection, phishing and fraud detection, anomaly detection, and encrypted traffic analysis, utilizing technologies such as OpenVINO™, vLLM.

title: Power Integrity Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The world is transforming - and so is Intel. Intel is a company of bold and curious inventors and problem solvers who create some of the most astounding technology advancements and experiences in the world. With a legacy of relentless innovation and a commitment to bring smart, connected devices to every person on Earth, our diverse and brilliant teams are continually searching for tomorrow's technology and revel in the challenge that changing the world for the better brings. We work every single day to design and manufacture silicon products that empower people's digital lives. Come join us and do something wonderful.


As a Power Integrity Engineer, you will contribute to the development and validation of power delivery solutions for complex, high-speed silicon, package, and platform designs. You will work with cross-functional engineering teams to analyze, optimize, and validate power delivery networks from silicon through package and board.

Your responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:
• Develop and analyze power delivery networks (PDNs) for silicon, packages, boards, and high-speed platforms.
• Perform 2D and 3D electromagnetic model extraction and power-noise analysis across the end-to-end power delivery path, including die/C4 bumps, package, socket, and board.
• Define and evaluate power-grid specifications, power-noise budgets, and design targets to balance power integrity, performance, area, and platform requirements.
• Apply power integrity principles and simulation methodologies to guide package and platform design and physical implementation.
• Analyze PDN impedance, voltage droop, resonance, ground bounce, decoupling effectiveness, and other power-noise characteristics.
• Develop electrical analysis methodologies, test structures, and verification plans for power delivery design and validation.
• Perform laboratory measurements to characterize power noise across frequency, transient response, ground bounce, and other key PDN metrics.
• Correlate post-silicon/platform measurements with pre-silicon simulations and models to improve design accuracy and methodology.
• Evaluate and optimize on-die, package, and platform decoupling strategies.
• Support voltage regulator (VR) performance characterization and optimization as part of the overall platform power delivery solution.
• Develop platform-level power delivery and decoupling recommendations for incorporation into platform design guides.
• Translate silicon power requirements into package and platform-level specifications and support design pathfinding to meet performance and form-factor requirements.
• Collaborate with silicon integration, die floorplanning, package, board/platform, voltage regulator, and validation teams to optimize the end-to-end power delivery solution.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience listed below would be obtained through a combination of your degree, research and or relevant previous job and or internship experiences.


Minimum Qualifications:
• Bachelor's in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, or a related STEM field & 1+ years of experience OR Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, or a related STEM field & 0+ years of experience.


• 1+ years of experience in one or more of the following areas:
Power integrity or power delivery.
Power electronics.
Signal integrity.
Voltage regulator design or validation.
PCB/package electrical modeling.
Electrical simulation.
Electrical laboratory testing or validation.

Preferred Qualifications:
The following qualifications are considered a plus:
• Experience with printed circuit board (PCB) and/or semiconductor package design and technology.
• Experience analyzing power delivery networks, including impedance, voltage-noise, transient-response, or decoupling behavior.
• Experience with electrical simulation, electromagnetic extraction, or high-speed design tools such as HSPICE, Ansys HFSS, Keysight ADS, Cadence PowerSI, or Cadence PowerDC.
• Knowledge of transmission-line theory, electromagnetic-field concepts, and passive component parasitics.
• Knowledge of voltage regulator operation, control, transient response, and interaction with platform-level power delivery networks.
• Experience using electrical laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, voltage/current probes, power supplies, and related measurement equipment.
• Experience correlating simulation results with laboratory measurements.
• Programming or scripting experience for engineering analysis and automation, such as Python, MATLAB, or similar tools.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and technical communication skills.

title: Power Delivery Integration and Power Rail Stress Engineer- SoC Power Thermal Performance Validation Engineer (Temporary position)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

As a SoC Power Thermal Performance Validation and Optimization Engineer, you will play an essential role in ensuring Intel's products achieve optimal power, thermal, and performance benchmarks at the system-on-chip (SoC) level.


In this position, you will develop and execute validation methodologies, optimize hardware/software solutions, and perform SoC-level debugging to address power, thermal, and performance challenges. Your contribution will directly impact Intel's ability to deliver competitive, high-performing products to market.

This is a Temporary position (12 months)


Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute System-on-Chip (SoC)-level power delivery, Power Rails Stress (PRS), maximum current (ICCmax), current transient (di/dt), minimum/maximum voltage (Vmin/Vmax), Digital Linear Voltage Regulator (DLVR)/Fully Integrated Voltage Regulator (FIVR), and concurrency plans, including feasibility study and design/verification/simulation of the Power Distribution Network (PDN) and sign-off of IR-drop/Electromigration (IR/EM) metrics, across Intel products.
  • Collaborate with architecture, design, firmware, software, Power Management architects, and layout teams to ensure power delivery meets competitive targets and specifications and to define and implement power gating solutions.
  • Establish and execute methodologies for validating hardware/software optimizations and to converge the design on all Power Distribution Network (PDN) metrics, ensuring alignment with business Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).
  • Perform System-on-Chip (SoC)-level debug to identify root causes and resolve functional and triage failures related to power delivery, on-die power grid/network, thermal, and performance.
  • Configure and set up data loggers to collect and analyze power/thermal data, and work with the package integration team to ensure the complete IP system meets the design specification.
  • Develop and maintain validation infrastructure (performance monitors, behavioral checkers, and testing environments) and work with the post-silicon debug team to triage, debug, and fix potential Power Distribution Network (PDN) issues.
  • Produce comprehensive validation reports summarizing activities and results and communicate findings effectively with relevant teams.
  • Drive continuous improvements to validation strategies, methodologies, and processes.

The ideal candidate should show the following behavioral traits

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Effective communication and documentation skills for cross-functional collaboration.
  • Advanced teamwork to work across teams in multi-faceted groups (architecture, design, verification, firmware, software, and platform teams).

Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications, you must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electronics, Electrical, Computer Engineering, or related field.
  • 1+ years of experience in System-on-Chip (SoC) power and performance validation and/or digital logic and optimization.
  • 1+ years of experience developing and / or optimization of power/performance Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and/or circuit design trade-off for power, performance, and area.
  • Intermediate to advanced English level.

Must have unrestricted, permanent right to work in Mexico (this role is not eligible for visa or immigration sponsorship).

Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

  • A master's degree is preferred.
  • Debugging experience for System-on-Chip (SoC)-level power, thermal, and performance failures.
  • Power Delivery design, implementation, and validation of high-performance and low-power designs.
  • Knowledge of hardware/software optimizations for power and performance.
  • Low power implementation techniques.
  • Experience with System-on-Chip (SoC)-level debug using Joint Test Action Group (JTAG) debuggers.
  • Familiarity with validation tools such as data acquisition/loggers, behavioral checkers, and state space coverage techniques.
  • Familiar with system board design/debugging and usage of lab equipment like Oscilloscope and Logic analyzer.
  • Experience with Power Delivery Integrity (PDI) validation infrastructure setup.
  • Experience with Python Programming language.

Requirements may be met through a combination of relevant industry experience, internship experience, and/or academic work, coursework, or research. Candidates who have completed their degree and whose professional experience is limited to internships may also be considered.

title: Director, Government Affairs - Taiwan
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role
Join Intel and help build a better tomorrow. Intel is in the midst of an exciting transformation, with a vision to create and extend computing technology that connects and enriches the lives of every person on Earth. Join us and help create the next generation of technologies that will shape the future for decades to come.
Intel's International Government Affairs team is seeking a dynamic and experienced leader to join our Taiwan team as Director of Government Affairs.
In this role, you will work closely with Intel Taiwan, the Director for Taiwan International Government Affairs ( IGA) and the Vice President of International Government Affairs to develop and execute a comprehensive government relations strategy that supports a favorable semiconductor policy and regulatory environment for Intel's growth and operations.
The Director will also be responsible for maintaining excellent relationships and networks with key government stakeholders at the national, prefectural, and local levels. This leader will play an important role in positively positioning Intel, building a sound reputation and position of influence for the company, and establishing Intel as a trusted and influential partner in Taiwan..

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

We are seeking an experienced Senior Robotics Solution Architect to define and develop end-to-end technical solutions for quadruped robotics. This role combines deep robotics domain expertise, hands-on engineering experience, and strong system architecture capabilities to translate customer requirements into scalable, deployable solutions leveraging Intel technologies. The successful candidate will work closely with robotics OEMs, ecosystem partners, and internal solutions and engineering teams to address architectural challenges across compute, AI, perception, planning, control, and software infrastructure. title: Senior Sales Operations Analyst
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact

Foundry Business Group Operations is seeking a highly analytical and strategic Senior Sales Operations Analyst to support forecasting, demand planning, and business operations for Intel Foundry customers. This role serves as a critical bridge between Business Development, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Finance, ensuring customer demand signals are translated into actionable business insights and operational plans.


As a key member of the Foundry Sales Operations team, you will drive forecast accuracy, demand visibility, and data-driven decision making across the sales lifecycle. You will analyze customer demand trends, identify business risks and opportunities, and partner with stakeholders to optimize capacity allocation, inventory strategies, and revenue attainment.

The ideal candidate combines strong analytical capabilities, semiconductor industry knowledge, and business acumen to influence strategic planning and operational execution. This role will also act as the primary operations interface for Front-End (FE) Wafer demand planning and forecasting activities supporting Intel Foundry customers.

Key Responsibilities

  • demand planning and forecasting processes for Intel Foundry customers, translating customer demand signals into actionable business plans.
  • Manage production demand forecasting using Blue Yonder CDP and engineering demand planning within SAP IBP.
  • Lead forecast reviews and demand planning cycles, ensuring alignment across Business Development, Strategy, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Finance stakeholders.
  • Partner with Business Development teams to establish forecasting readiness for new products, including product setup, demand assumptions, and lifecycle planning.
  • Support Sales and Operations Planning (S&OP) and Long-Range Planning (LRP) processes by developing data-driven demand scenarios and identifying planning assumptions, risks, and opportunities.

  • Develop executive-level reporting and dashboards that provide visibility into demand, capacity utilization, inventory health, and revenue opportunities.
  • Monitor forecast performance, including forecast accuracy, bias, and lag indicators, and recommend corrective actions.
  • Collaborate with Supply Chain and Manufacturing teams to align demand forecasts with available capacity, inventory strategies, and supply commitments.
  • Partner with Customer Business Analysts to maintain accurate customer rolling forecasts and demand visibility.
  • Strong stakeholder management and cross-functional collaboration skills.
  • Identify operational constraints, capacity gaps, and customer fulfillment risks, proactively driving mitigation strategies.
  • Support new product introductions (NPI), engineering builds, high-volume manufacturing (HVM) ramps, and customer milestone execution.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance forecasting methodologies, planning processes, data quality, and operational efficiency.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Finance, Operations, Bachelor of Arts or in a similar field.
  • 6+ years of experience in Sales Operations, Demand Planning, Supply Chain Analytics, Business Planning, or Capacity Planning within semiconductor or advanced manufacturing environments.

  • Experience with Sales and Operations Planning (S&OP), Integrated Business Planning (IBP), or related planning methodologies.
  • Proficiency with ERP and planning systems such as SAP IBP, Blue Yonder, or similar enterprise planning tools.

title: Memory IP Architect
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact

As a Memory IP Architect, you will lead the definition and development of advanced digital IP architectures that power Intel's next-generation semiconductor solutions. You will be responsible for creating scalable, configurable, and high-performance IP designs while driving innovations in functionality, power efficiency, performance, and silicon area optimization. Working closely with architecture, design, verification, and SoC teams, you will influence critical technology decisions and help shape the future of Intel's portfolio.  

About the Team 

The Intel Foundry FUSE Design Team develops advanced digital IP solutions that enable seamless integration across a broad range of products and platforms. Our team focuses on creating highly configurable and reusable IP architectures that accelerate innovation, improve product scalability, and deliver industry-leading performance. As part of Intel Foundry, you will contribute to technologies that power the next generation of computing and semiconductor solutions worldwide. 

Key Responsibilities 

  • Define, develop, and drive digital IP architecture specifications with a focus on modularity, configurability, performance, power efficiency, and area optimization. 
  • Lead architecture exploration activities, evaluating trade-offs and proposing innovative solutions for next-generation IP designs. 
  • Develop microarchitecture concepts and architectural features, including modeling and simulation to evaluate performance, power, and area metrics. 
  • Analyze validation and test data, leveraging statistical methods to identify optimization opportunities and improve IP quality. 
  • Partner with design, verification, validation, and product engineering teams to ensure successful architecture implementation and execution. 
  • Evaluate design alternatives and validate IP configurations, connectivity, interoperability, and overall system performance. 
  • Collaborate with SoC architects and integration teams to support IP selection, integration, performance tuning, and system-level validation. 
  • Drive technical innovation by identifying emerging technologies, methodologies, and architectural approaches that enhance Intel's IP portfolio. 

What You'll Bring 

  • Strong technical leadership with the ability to influence cross-functional engineering teams. 
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with experience working across architecture, design, verification, and product organizations. 
  • Proven problem-solving capabilities and a passion for developing innovative technical solutions. 
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment while managing complex technical challenges and competing priorities. 
  • A growth mindset with a commitment to continuous learning and technology advancement. 

Qualifications:

title: 3DIC Device Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Team

Manufacturing Development and Customer Engineering (MDCE) serves as the critical bridge between Technology Development (TD) and High Volume Manufacturing (HVM) within Intel Foundry. The organization is responsible for transitioning leading-edge technologies from development and qualification into high-yield production while enabling successful deployment for foundry customers.


The MDCE Device Team is expanding its 3DIC device engineering capabilities and is seeking an experienced engineer to drive device understanding and optimization for advanced 3D integration technologies.


Position Overview

As a 3DIC Device Development Engineer, you will be responsible for understanding, characterizing, and modeling the impact of advanced 3D integration technologies on transistor and passive device performance. Technologies such as through-silicon vias (TSVs), hybrid bonding, active base die architectures, wafer thinning, and backside power delivery introduce new mechanical, thermal, and electrical interactions that influence device behavior, variability, and reliability.


In this role, you will transform complex silicon data into actionable insights, design rules, device collateral, and customer-ready guidance that support next-generation products including AI accelerators, high-performance computing solutions, and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) platforms.


Key Responsibilities


Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Characterize and model the impact of advanced 3D integration technologies, including TSVs, hybrid bonding, wafer thinning, and backside processing, on device performance metrics such as mobility, threshold voltage (Vt), leakage, matching, and variability.
  • Evaluate stress, thermal, and electrical coupling effects, including keep-out zone (KOZ) behavior and device interactions within complex 3D stacks.
  • Define and develop device and passive test structures to study 3DIC effects, including TSV proximity, KOZ, guard ring, resistor, and capacitor structures.
  • Drive electrical test (e-test) strategy, data collection, and silicon analysis to accelerate technology learning and optimization.
  • Provide device characterization inputs that enable design rule development, compact models, PDKs, and 3D design kit releases in collaboration with Design Enablement teams.
  • Partner closely with Process Integration, Packaging, Assembly, Reliability, Yield, and Program Management organizations to identify, troubleshoot, and resolve device-related issues.
  • Evaluate customer requirements for analog, mixed-signal, RF, and high-speed I/O devices within 3D architectures, assessing technical feasibility, risk, and implementation timelines.
  • Support technology qualification and manufacturing readiness activities, including device targeting, monitoring strategies, yield improvement efforts, and excursion management.
  • Communicate complex technical findings and recommendations to engineering, business, and customer stakeholders.

What We Are Looking For


The successful candidate will demonstrate:

  • Deep understanding of CMOS device physics and the impact of process, stress, and thermal effects on device performance.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including data science, statistical analysis, and scripting capabilities.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to diverse audiences.
  • Proven ability to influence and collaborate across device, process, packaging, manufacturing, and design organizations.
  • Strong ownership mindset, technical curiosity, and a passion for developing innovative solutions in advanced semiconductor technologies.

Qualifications:

The Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position.  Minimum qualifications listed below would be obtained through a combination of industry relevant job experience, internship experience and / or schoolwork/classes/research. The preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.


Minimum Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Materials Science, or a related field with 4+ years of industry experience, in semiconductor device engineering, process integration, advanced packaging, or related technology development.
  • 3+ years of experience in advanced CMOS device characterization and electrical parametric (e-test) data analysis.
  • Hands-on experience with one or more advanced packaging and 3D integration technologies, including:
    • Through-silicon vias (TSVs)
    • Hybrid bonding
    • Wafer-to-wafer or die-to-wafer bonding
    • Micro-bump technologies
    • Wafer thinning
    • Backside power delivery

Preferred Qualifications

  • PhD in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Materials Science, or a related field.
  • Experience analyzing stress and thermal interactions affecting device behavior, including TSV keep-out zones and chip-package interaction effects.
  • Expertise in test structure development, design of experiments (DOE), and e-test program implementation.
  • Knowledge of device modeling, design rule development, PDK generation, or design technology co-optimization (DTCO).
  • Experience using TCAD and/or finite element analysis tools for stress, thermal, or device simulations.
  • Understanding of semiconductor reliability mechanisms, including electromigration (EM), time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB), bias temperature instability (BTI), and bonding interface reliability.
  • Experience with advanced node technologies, including FinFET and Gate-All-Around (GAA) devices.
  • Semiconductor foundry experience with direct customer engagement and technical support.
  • Experience supporting technology transfer and production ramp in high-volume manufacturing environments.

Join us in shaping the future of semiconductor innovation through advanced 3D integration technologies that enable the next generation of AI, HPC, and memory solutions.

title: Intel Foundry Module Development Engineer - CMP Metrology
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Join Intel and help create the technologies that will shape the future of computing. Intel's Logic Technology Development organization is advancing the next generation of semiconductor technology by solving challenges at the leading edge of physics, materials, and manufacturing. As device dimensions become smaller and performance requirements become more demanding, our engineers continue to push beyond what was previously thought possible.

The Chemical Mechanical Planarization team is seeking a Development Engineer to build and advance the measurement capabilities that make these breakthroughs possible. Metrology provides the insight needed to understand complex semiconductor structures, guide process development, and deliver the precision required for increasingly sophisticated devices.

This role brings together optical science, semiconductor processing, data analytics, automation, and manufacturing engineering. You will join a collaborative, multidisciplinary team that turns challenging measurement problems into scalable solutions for technology development and high-volume manufacturing, helping transform new ideas into the next generation of computing products.

The role's responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Drive the development of breakthrough optical metrology solutions for leading-edge semiconductor technologies
  • Qualify metrology hardware, models, and recipes for production use in high volume manufacturing
  • Own fleet health and tool-to-tool matching to ensure reliable operations
  • Pursue line variation reduction targets by employing advanced process control techniques
  • Build scalable business processes that streamline engineering activities and accelerate decision making
  • Enable high-volume manufacturing with robust controls and clear documentation
  • Equip engineers to use and sustain the systems
  • Lead engineering teams and suppliers to solve complex technical challenges
  • Shape the metrology roadmap and champion next-generation capabilities

Qualifications:

You must possess the minimum qualifications below to be initially considered for this position. Qualifications may be obtained through a combination of industry-relevant job experience, internships, coursework, or research.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or a related STEM (Science Technology Engineering Math) field of study with 4+ years of Semiconductor Industry experience (semiconductor processing and semiconductor fabrication)

OR

  • Master's degree in Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or a related STEM field of study with 3+ years of Semiconductor Industry experience (semiconductor processing and semiconductor fabrication)

OR

  • PhD degree in Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or a related STEM field of study with 6+ months of experience of Semiconductor Industry experience (semiconductor processing and semiconductor fabrication)

Experience in Semiconductor Industry (semiconductor processing and semiconductor fabrication) includes one or more of the following:

  • Optical science
  • Semiconductor processing
  • Data analytics
  • Factory automation
  • Manufacturing engineering

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Hands-on experience developing and sustaining thin-film optical metrology recipes and models in semiconductor development or high-volume manufacturing
  • Knowledge of optical spectroscopy, spectroscopic ellipsometry, reflectometry, or electromagnetic modeling of multilayer film stacks
  • Experience interpreting optical spectra and correlating model output with reference measurement and physical cross-sections
  • Experience with metrology capability analysis, including precision, matching, stability, and measurement uncertainty
  • Working knowledge of CMP process fundamentals and the relationship between film-stack geometry, planarization, and thickness targets
  • Experience applying Statistical Process Control, Design of Experiments, fault detection, or model-health monitoring
  • Data analysis skills using JMP, Python, SQL, or comparable tools
  • Experience managing engineering change control for metrology hardware, models, or recipes
  • Demonstrated success working across engineering organizations and with equipment or software suppliers
  • Ability to translate complex technical results into concise, actionable information for technical audiences

  • Partner with physical-design/backend teams on pre- and post-physical-design timing and power convergence.
  • Work closely with verification teams to review test plans and assertions, debug RTL and gate-level simulation failures, and drive corrective actions.
  • Collaborate with DFT, structural design, full-chip validation, architecture, and IP-provider teams to ensure smooth IP-to-SoC handoff and convergence.
  • Provide technical leadership by setting priorities, driving results across organizational boundaries, mentoring engineers, and fostering an inclusive and collaborative work environment.

The ideal candidate is a self-motivated technical leader with strong problem-solving, communication, and organizational skills who can operate effectively in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment.

title: C4 Bump Module Equipment Technician
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Join Intel Malaysia's newest Advanced Packaging startup team in Penang and help shape the future of semiconductor manufacturing. As part of a factory ramp from the ground up, you will work with advanced wafer manufacturing and packaging technologies, collaborate with global engineering teams, and play a key role in bringing new capabilities into high-volume production. This unique opportunity offers unparalleled exposure to factory startup activities, rapid professional growth, and the chance to leave your mark on one of Intel's most significant manufacturing expansions.


Job Summary

  • The Equipment Technician plays a critical role in the startup, ramp, and sustained operation of advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment supporting high-volume Advanced Packaging production.
  • This position is responsible for maintaining equipment performance, reliability, and availability through troubleshooting, preventive maintenance, equipment recovery, and continuous improvement activities.
  • The Equipment Technician partners closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Facilities, and equipment suppliers to support manufacturing readiness, operational excellence, yield, quality, and factory output while ensuring compliance with safety, environmental, and quality requirements.
  • Performs electrical, mechanical, electronic, and/or mechatronic troubleshooting to identify and resolve problems with semiconductor manufacturing equipment.
  • Performs equipment setup, calibration, preventive maintenance, repair, adjustment, component replacement, and equipment recovery in accordance with approved procedures, specifications, equipment manuals, drawings, and safety requirements.
  • Monitors and analyzes equipment performance and manufacturing data to identify abnormalities, equipment degradation, and conditions that may affect equipment availability, process stability, manufacturing output, yield, or product quality.
  • Responds to equipment alarms, equipment-related excursions, and manufacturing interruptions in accordance with established procedures to restore equipment to required operating conditions.
  • Collects relevant equipment data, performs authorized troubleshooting, and works with Equipment, Module, and Process Engineering teams to identify root causes and implement corrective actions.
  • Performs routine equipment health monitoring and supports the early identification of equipment conditions or trends that could impact manufacturing performance, reliability, capacity, or manufacturing readiness.
  • Works with Engineering teams to execute approved experiments, equipment characterization, process qualifications, equipment configuration changes, and continuous improvement initiatives. Supports equipment troubleshooting through data analysis, root cause investigation, and controlled experimentation to maintain or improve equipment availability, reliability, performance, and manufacturing readiness.
  • Supports established Statistical Process Control (SPC), equipment monitoring, fault detection, and manufacturing control systems by responding to equipment-related abnormalities according to defined procedures and escalation requirements.
  • Utilizes equipment performance data and system indicators to proactively identify opportunities for improved equipment stability and operational performance.
  • Coordinates with OEMs, equipment suppliers, and technical support organizations for troubleshooting, repair, servicing, component replacement, equipment recovery, and reliability improvements when required.
  • Works closely with Equipment Engineering, Process Engineering, Manufacturing, Facilities, and other support teams to resolve equipment-related manufacturing issues and support production objectives.
  • Creates and maintains equipment failure reports, maintenance records, troubleshooting documentation, calibration records, qualification records, and other technical documentation supporting equipment performance, reliability, and compliance requirements.
  • During factory startup and ramp, supports equipment installation, acceptance, setup, conversion, qualification, and manufacturing readiness activities in accordance with approved designs, specifications, and procedures.
  • Contributes to the successful introduction of new equipment, technologies, and manufacturing capabilities supporting Advanced Packaging operations.
  • Drives a culture of safety, quality, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.
  • Performs assigned work in accordance with applicable EHS, cleanroom, quality, contamination control, and manufacturing work-control requirements.

Qualifications:

Education

  • Diploma in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Automation Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

Experience

  • Fresh graduates with strong technical aptitude and an interest in semiconductor manufacturing are encouraged to apply.
  • Relevant experience in semiconductor manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, electronics manufacturing, equipment maintenance, equipment troubleshooting, automation, or other high-volume manufacturing environments is an advantage.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with semiconductor manufacturing equipment troubleshooting, preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, repair, setup, calibration, and equipment recovery.
  • Familiarity with semiconductor wafer fabrication, Advanced Packaging, assembly, test, or other high-volume manufacturing processes and equipment.
  • Familiarity with equipment and process monitoring methodologies, including Statistical Process Control (SPC), equipment performance monitoring, excursion management, and data-driven problem solving.
  • Experience interpreting equipment alarms, diagnostic information, technical documentation, schematics, engineering drawings, specifications, maintenance procedures, and equipment manuals.
  • Familiarity with structured troubleshooting methodologies, failure analysis, root cause investigation, and implementation of corrective actions.
  • Experience supporting equipment installation, startup, qualification, manufacturing readiness, production ramp, or equipment conversion activities is an added advantage.
  • Familiarity with automated material handling systems (AMHS), robotics, wafer handling systems, process equipment, metrology tools, automation platforms, manufacturing execution systems (MES), and manufacturing control systems is an added advantage.
  • Experience working with OEMs, suppliers, or technical service organizations to support equipment troubleshooting and maintenance activities is an added advantage.

Other Requirements

  • Strong technical aptitude and systematic problem-solving skills.
  • Basic understanding of mechanical, electrical, electronic, automation, pneumatic, vacuum, and/or mechatronic systems.
  • Basic understanding of semiconductor manufacturing operations and the relationship between equipment condition, process stability, yield, manufacturing performance, and product quality.
  • Ability to interpret and follow technical documentation, equipment manuals, schematics, specifications, maintenance procedures, and work instructions.
  • Ability to identify abnormal equipment or manufacturing conditions and respond or escalate in accordance with established procedures.
  • Strong communication and teamwork skills, including the ability to collaborate effectively with Engineering, Manufacturing, Facilities, OEMs, suppliers, and cross-functional support teams.
  • Demonstrated learning agility and the ability to quickly acquire proficiency on new equipment, manufacturing processes, automation systems, and technologies.
  • Attention to detail and commitment to safety, quality, equipment reliability, and operational excellence.
  • Willing and able to work in a semiconductor cleanroom environment while adhering to contamination control, safety, and quality requirements.
  • Demonstrated flexibility and willingness to support factory startup, equipment installation, qualification, production ramp, and evolving manufacturing requirements in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
  • This role requires regular onsite presence to fulfill essential job responsibilities.
  • Willing and able to work shift schedules, including rotating day and night shifts, as required to support manufacturing operations.
  • Able to support overtime, weekends, public holidays, factory startup, production ramp, and equipment recovery activities based on business and manufacturing requirements.

title: Semiconductor Research Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

As a Semiconductor Research Engineer, you will drive hands-on research and competency development to advance Intel's future assembly packaging platform technologies. Using CFD/FEA simulation, you will define electronic packaging manufacturability and design optimization windows, solving complex technical challenges and delivering high-impact solutions that support Intel's technology roadmap.

Business Group
You will join the Advanced Design and Customer Enabling group in Intel Foundry, a global semiconductor manufacturing leader driving design innovation and high-density electronic packaging. The group leverages cutting-edge materials, processes, and computational techniques to deliver advanced packaging assembly technologies.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and implement Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) and Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulations for electronic packaging design assessment, and conduct research and core competency development to build predictive capabilities.
  • Apply scientific principles to develop and assess novel electronic packaging concepts ahead of physical prototyping till high volume manufacturing.
  • Build prototypes and conduct lab-scale experiments for visualization and validation.
  • Conduct parametric studies and propose innovative solutions for design optimization and performance improvement.
  • Lead external vendor engagements and mentor academic and industry research collaborations.

Qualifications:

  • Master's degree with 1 to 2 years of relevant experience or
  • PhD in Mechanical Engineering with expertise in CFD or FEA, and experience in design parametric studies and electronic packaging. Fresh graduates are encouraged to apply.
  • Proficiency in Fluent, Ansys, Abaqus, Python, MATLAB, and VS Code for analysis tool automation and AI integration.
  • Familiarity with design of experiments (DOE) and materials characterization techniques.
  • Fundamental understanding of flip-chip and advanced packaging anatomy and assembly processes.
  • Strong communication and collaborative problem-solving skills.
  • Experience in external collaborations and academic mentorship.
  • Hands-on research capability with disciplined execution and clear research vision.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact

We are seeking a skilled Power Integrity Engineer to join our team and contribute to the development of advanced power delivery solutions. In this role, you will analyze, design, and verify power integrity networks across silicon, packages, and platforms, ensuring optimal performance and functionality. Your work will directly impact product quality and reliability, enabling Intel to deliver state-of-the-art solutions that meet the demands of next-generation technology.


Business group

title: Junior CPU Verification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Who We Are

At Intel, we are shaping the future of computing. Our engineering teams develop the technologies that power billions of devices worldwide, from personal computers and cloud infrastructure to edge computing and artificial intelligence applications.


Join Intel's CPU Design team and become part of a world-class engineering organization responsible for designing and verifying next-generation processor technologies. As a Junior CPU Verification Engineer, you will work alongside experienced architects, designers, and verification engineers to ensure the quality, functionality, and performance of Intel's future CPU products.


The Role

As a CPU Verification Engineer, you will be responsible for verifying complex processor designs before they reach silicon. You will develop verification environments, create test plans, debug failures, and collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure Intel CPUs meet functional, performance, power, and quality objectives.


What You’ll Do

Responsibilities may include but are not limited to:


  • Performs functional verification of CPU logic to ensure design will meet specification requirements.
  • Develops IP verification plans, test benches, and the verification environment to ensure coverage to confirm to CPU microarchitecture specifications.
  • Executes verification plans and defines and runs system simulation models to verify the design, analyze power and timing, and uncover bugs.
  • Replicates, root causes, and debugs issues in the presilicon environment.
  • Finds and implements corrective measures to resolve failing tests.
  • Collaborates with CPU architects, RTL developers, and physical design teams to improve verification of complex architectural and microarchitectural features and to meet functional, performance, and power goals.
  • Documents test plans and drive technical reviews of plans and proofs with design and architecture teams.
  • Maintains and improves existing functional verification infrastructure and methodology.
  • Participates in the definition of architecture and microarchitecture features of the CPU being designed actively.

Behavioral traits that we are looking for:

  • Strong analytical thinking and a passion for solving complex technical challenges.
  • Curiosity and eagerness to continuously learn new technologies, tools, and methodologies.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Effective collaboration and teamwork across multidisciplinary engineering organizations.
  • Ability to balance attention to detail while understanding broader system impacts.
  • Adaptability and resilience in a fast-paced technical environment.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills.
  • A growth mindset and openness to feedback and continuous improvement.

Why Intel

At Intel, your work will have real-world impact from day one. You'll collaborate with industry-leading engineers, gain mentorship from technical experts, and contribute to cutting-edge processor technologies that enable the next generation of computing.


Whether you're passionate about computer architecture, hardware design, verification methodologies, or emerging AI technologies, Intel provides an environment where you can grow your career while solving some of the industry's most challenging engineering problems.


If you're excited by complex technical challenges and eager to help shape the future of computing, we encourage you to apply.


Intel invests in our people and offers a complete and competitive package of benefits employees and their families through every stage of life.

title: Device Engineer
descriptionHtml:

Job Description: 

Intel Ireland Device Engineering team (Yield department) is looking for Device Engineering talents (reporting to manger of Device team) to join our advanced technology Fab.

As a Device Engineer/Senior Device Engineer, you will focus on most advanced FinFETs technology device engineering/development working closely with Integration, Module, yield teams to achieve yield ramp-up, process and device optimization in the high-volume manufacturing Fab, supporting internal and external customers.

Own NPI (New Product Introduction) in production fab and perform device-related process optimizations to meet foundry customers product specifications and requirements.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Life at Intel

As an AI Frameworks Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in designing and developing cutting-edge AI software to optimize AI frameworks. On a practical day-to-day level, you will contribute to the development and optimization of advanced AI frameworks, implement distributed algorithms, and collaborate with researchers to deliver high-performance solutions. Your work will directly enhance Intel's AI capabilities and drive innovation in machine learning and deep learning technologies.

Business Group
At Intel Corporation, our teams are dedicated to pushing the boundaries of technology to create world-changing innovations.   • Design, develop, and optimize AI frameworks such as OpenVINO, TensorFlow, and PyTorch.

  • Optimize code across a variety of computing hardware backends to maximize performance.

  • Strong communication and presentation skills.

title: Team Amazon | AWS Cloud GTM Sales Director
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Opportunity

Amazon operates at extraordinary scale across cloud, retail, devices, advertising, logistics, and emerging businesses. Intel technology contributes across that landscape, from developer PCs and edge systems to the infrastructure supporting cloud services and customer workloads.

Team Amazon is looking for a highly motivated, customer-obsessed leader to serve as Intel's AWS Cloud Go-To-Market Sales Director. This commissioned sales role leads Sales Development Account Managers who help AWS sellers, partners, ISVs, and end customers translate business challenges into scalable cloud and AI outcomes.

Your success will not be measured by pipeline alone. It will be measured by the customer problems solved, trust earned, workloads modernized, adoption expanded, and durable value created for customers, AWS, and Intel. You will own quarterly and annual deal commitments, regional demand forecasting, new service and solution development, investment effectiveness, and long-term customer success.

This is a high-energy role for a leader who can think big, dive deep, move with speed, and stay close to the details. You will influence Intel business units and executive leaders with direct customer insight, shaping roadmaps, strategy, and operating mechanisms around what customers need next.

What You Will Own

• Start with the customer. Build a deep understanding of customer business priorities, technical constraints, buying journeys, and measures of success. Work backward from the desired outcome rather than forward from a product.
• Earn and keep trust. Establish durable relationships with customer executives, technical leaders, AWS sellers, partners, and ISVs. Listen carefully, communicate candidly, follow through, and represent customer needs accurately inside Intel.
• Turn insight into action. Convert customer signals into clear account strategies, solution plays, roadmap input, and field mechanisms. Ensure customer feedback reaches the teams that can act on it.
• Create customer value at scale. Build and scale a substantial pipeline of customers consuming Intel-based AWS services, with emphasis on net-new workloads, cloud migration, modernization, AI, data, and industry solutions.
• Lead the full customer journey. Drive opportunities from discovery through validation, commercial alignment, launch, adoption, and expansion. Remove friction across organizational boundaries and remain accountable for outcomes after the deal closes.
• Invent and simplify. Create repeatable GTM motions, decision frameworks, enablement, and operating mechanisms that make it easier for AWS teams and customers to choose, deploy, and optimize the right solutions.
• Think big and prioritize. Set a bold, customer-led vision for Intel cloud GTM while making disciplined choices about where the team, investments, and executive attention can create the greatest customer impact.
• Use investment as a customer-value lever. Manage a global multi-million-dollar investment budget with clear hypotheses, guardrails, and success measures tied to customer adoption, business impact, and repeatability.
• Dive deep and deliver results. Maintain rigorous pipeline inspection, forecasting, business reviews, and post-investment measurement. Reconcile metrics with customer evidence and act quickly when they diverge.
• Build leaders. Hire, coach, and develop a high-performing team that demonstrates ownership, curiosity, sound judgment, high standards, and an instinct to serve the customer.
• Operate as one team. Mobilize direct staff, regional sellers, Intel account teams, AWS account and specialist teams, partners, and funded roles around a shared customer plan and clear ownership.
• Stay close to the customer. Spend significant time with customers and field stakeholders.


The role is expected to involve approximately fifty percent travel. This role is based in Seattle.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualification:
• Outstanding communication skills and the ability to engage and influence all levels both internally and externally.
• Proven ability to lead and manage direct and cross-functional teams.
• Thrive in a fast paced, collaborative and, at times, ambiguous environment. Coordinate with the right resources to get the job done, take ownership or delegate where appropriate.
• Sales experience with Cloud, AI, Edge and/or Networking products.
• Success in complicated business and partnership negotiations.

Preferred Qualifications:
• In depth knowledge of Amazon, the industry trends around hyperscalers and partnership business models.
• 5+ years of sales and relationship management with a track record of growth with large accounts.
• Strong knowledge of Data Center and AI strategies and technology.
• Sales experience with Amazon/AWS and the capability to influence the technical and commercial benefits of building solutions on Intel platforms and technologies.
• Continued learning certifications: AWS Cloud Practitioner, AWS Solution Architect, AWS AI Practitioner.

title: Manufacturing Equipment Technician (MTE) - Day Shift 7
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel Foundry is a first-of-its-kind, systems-focused foundry, leading the transition toward a highly connected, silicon-driven global economy. Our dynamic team is dedicated to delivering world-class semiconductor manufacturing solutions that support Intel's broader mission of enabling transformative computing experiences. We collaborate across engineering and manufacturing sectors to sustain tool performance, accelerate factory ramps, and enable seamless, high-volume manufacturing.

We are seeking a highly motivated, hands-on Module Equipment Technician to join our team in Chandler, Arizona. In this role, you will play a critical part in sustaining the reliability, performance, and uptime of advanced manufacturing toolsets. Working on-site in a highly technical cleanroom environment, you will troubleshoot complex electromechanical systems, perform routine preventive maintenance, and partner with Engineering to execute critical equipment configurations and factory installations.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Diagnose & Repair: Troubleshoot and resolve electrical, mechanical, pneumatic, and hydraulic issues on complex manufacturing hardware.
  • Interpret Technical Schematics: Dismantle, adjust, repair, and assemble machinery utilizing blueprint layouts, electrical schematics, operating manuals, and technical drawings.
  • Tool Setup & Metrology: Conduct equipment setups, multi-point calibrations, and scheduled preventive maintenance, coordinating with suppliers for specialized services.
  • Failure Reporting: Document system failures and write detailed maintenance reports, helping update operational specifications to increase tool performance.
  • Engineering Experimentation: Collaborate with Module Engineering to implement tool configuration changes, collect experimental data, and execute test procedures.
  • Factory Ramp Support: Partner with construction and installation teams during factory expansion phases to ensure proper tool installation, leveling, and hook-up per design layout.

As a Successful Candidate, You Will Bring:

  • Analytical Problem Solver: Logical mindset geared toward systematic troubleshooting, interpreting logs, and diagnosing complex issues.
  • Adaptable & Self-Motivated: Thrives under minimal supervision in a fast-paced environment with rapidly shifting priorities.
  • Collaborative Partner: Team player who works seamlessly alongside engineers, supplier representatives, and construction crews.
  • Rigorous & Precision-Focused: High attention to detail with an uncompromised commitment to cleanroom quality standards and safety protocols.
  • Clear Communicator: Strong written and verbal communication skills to document repairs, update specs, and coordinate shift handoffs.

The TD QnR Failure Analysis and Fault Isolation (FAFI) organization is seeking a highly motivated Electrical Failure Analysis Engineer to join the Nanoprobing Engineering (NPE) team on Shift 2. FAFI serves as the technical forensic organization responsible for identifying, isolating, and understanding electrical failures impacting next-generation semiconductor technologies and products. As a Nanoprobing Engineer, you will utilize advanced electrical characterization and nanoprobing techniques to investigate device, transistor, circuit, and product-level reliability and yield challenges across leading-edge CMOS technologies. This position provides an opportunity to work at the intersection of semiconductor device physics, circuit design, reliability engineering, and advanced failure analysis. Engineers in this role develop innovative debug methodologies and perform detailed electrical investigations to enable rapid root-cause determination and technology learning. Responsibilities Perform advanced nanoprobing investigations to identify and isolate electrical failure mechanisms in leading-edge semiconductor technologies. Execute cell-level, transistor-level, SRAM, logic, and analog circuit characterization activities using state-of-the-art nanoprobing platforms. Analyze electrical signatures to determine root causes associated with reliability, performance, yield, and functional failures. Develop and improve characterization methodologies for transistor and circuit-level validation. Utilize semiconductor parameter analyzers, waveform generators, oscilloscopes, and switching systems to perform precision electrical measurements. Correlate nanoprobing results with fault isolation, physical failure analysis, design, process, and reliability data. Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Design, Process Integration, Device Engineering, Reliability, Product Engineering, and Failure Analysis organizations. Drive technical problem solving and debug efforts on complex issues involving advanced CMOS technologies. Document findings and communicate technical results through reports, presentations, and engineering reviews. Support development and deployment of next-generation electrical characterization and failure analysis capabilities.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications
Master's degree in: Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Engineering Physics Applied Physics Or a closely related technical discipline.

Strong understanding of semiconductor device physics.
Strong understanding of electronic circuits and circuit analysis.

Preferred Qualifications
Experience in one or more of the following areas:
Nanoprobing or electrical failure analysis.
Semiconductor parameter analyzer operation.
Device characterization and transistor measurements.
CMOS process technology and semiconductor manufacturing.
Digital circuit design and debug.
SRAM, memory, or logic circuit characterization.
Reliability testing and root-cause analysis.
Fault isolation techniques.
Analog or mixed-signal characterization.
Python, MATLAB, or data analysis programming.
Linux/Unix environments.
Statistical data analysis and automation development.

Ideal Candidate
The successful candidate will be a hands-on experimental engineer who enjoys solving complex technical challenges. They will possess strong laboratory skills, a passion for semiconductor technology, and the ability to translate electrical observations into actionable failure analysis conclusions. The ideal applicant is comfortable working in a fast-paced environment where every failure presents a unique technical investigation requiring creativity, persistence, and rigorous analytical thinking.

title: Transistor Reliability and Quality Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel is seeking a highly motivated and talented Transistor Quality and Reliability Engineer to join our Technology Development Quality and Reliability Engineering team. In this role, you will work at the cutting edge of transistor technology development, ensuring the highest levels of quality and reliability for Intel's next-generation process technologies. You will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams including Process Integration, Device Engineering, Yield Engineering, and Product teams to drive quality and reliability excellence from early technology development through technology qualification and high-volume manufacturing readiness. Responsibilities - Drive transistor reliability characterization and certification activities including but not limited to: Hot Carrier Injection (HCI), Bias Temperature Instability (NBTI/PBTI), Time Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) - Collaborate with process integration and device engineering teams to develop a high volume manufacturable technology that meets yield, performance and reliability requirements. o Develop FMEA for novel transistor structures and materials o Define and implement reliability monitors and early warning indicators for technologies o Drive continuous improvement in reliability methodologies, test structures, and characterization techniques - Develop physics-based and empirical reliability models for transistor wear-out and degradation mechanisms including: o Lifetime prediction o Statistical distribution modeling (Weibull, lognormal) o SPICE-compatible reliability model development for circuit design enablement - Design reliability test structures and test-chip layouts to enable: o Systematic reliability characterization o Early detection of reliability and quality risks o Collaboration with layout and design teams to tape-in test-structures and influence design for reliability for partner organizations - Develop and improve automation framework for data analysis to enable: o Systematic reliability characterization from a high volume of data across multi variable process modulators

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications - Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, or a related field with 6+ years of industry experience OR a Master's degree in the above fields with 4+ years of experience OR a Ph.D. with 2+ years of experience. - Hands-on experience in semiconductor device fabrication, process characterization, and experimental design. - Proficiency in statistical analysis and data interpretation using tools such as JMP, R, SAS, or Python. - Strong technical background in semiconductor device physics and reliability mechanisms. - Knowledge of process integration and technology development methodologies. Preferred Qualifications - Experience in semiconductor reliability engineering and technology qualification frameworks. - Familiarity with advanced CMOS process integration and transistor reliability mechanisms (e.g., HTOL, ELFR, TDDB). - Proficiency in statistical quality systems, process capability analysis, and defect reliability modeling. - Background in data analytics, machine learning, and AI-assisted engineering workflows. - Expertise in semiconductor failure analysis, fabrication, and physical characterization techniques. - Experience with automation and scripting tools such as SQL and Python. We're looking for exceptional candidates eager to make a lasting impact on Intel's innovation journey.
