title: Senior Capacity and Strategic Planning Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

CapEx LRP Capacity leader. Will lead financial planning and management of capital-related costs across the Long-Range Planning process. This role will serve as the key connection between capacity and financial planning, ensuring that different capacity and technology scenarios are translated into clear, accurate, and actionable CapEx outlooks. The position will work closely with Finance, FCS, FCSP, and other cross-functional stakeholders to establish a consistent CapEx methodology, set capex guardrails for yearly spending, improve financial visibility, and support strategic decision-making. Key responsibilities : 1.Own the LRP CapEx mapping and forecasting process, translating long-range capacity plans into capital requirements and financial outlooks. 2.Develop a clear understanding of CapEx cost by technology node, capacity increment, site, and major investment driver 3.Quantify the CapEx impact of alternative capacity scenarios, including changes in demand, ramp timing, capacity additions, pull-ins/push-outs, and network optimization decisions. 4.Partner closely with Finance, FCS, FCSP, and planning stakeholders to ensure alignment between capacity assumptions and financial forecasts. 5.Build and maintain a clean financial walk explaining changes between planning cycles, including volume, capacity, technology, timing, and other key CapEx drivers. 6.Develop scalable tools, models, dashboards, and processes that improve CapEx forecasting accuracy, transparency, traceability, and efficiency. 7.Establish clear assumptions, baselines, and change-control mechanisms to ensure consistency across LRP scenarios. Identify financial risks, opportunities, gaps, and inconsistencies early and drive cross-functional resolution. 8.Translate complex capacity and financial information into clear executive-level insights, trade-offs, and recommendations. 9.Drive continuous improvement and standardization of the LRP CapEx planning process

- Strong Finance, capital planning, business planning, or equivalent financial background.

- Experience developing planning tools, automation, dashboards, or Power BI capabilities is highly desirable.
- Strong program management skills with exceptional attention to detail and organizational discipline.
- Ability to manage multiple scenarios, assumptions, stakeholders, and planning cycles in parallel.

title: Senior CPU Logic Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

As part of Intel's Core Engineering Group, we develop Intel's next-generation high-IPC CPU cores, powering client, server, cloud, and emerging AI platforms.

Our cores are among Intel's most strategic and sophisticated IPs, enabling products deployed at hyperscale and in hundreds of millions of systems worldwide. We are seeking experienced CPU designers to help define and implement the next generation of high-performance CPU technologies.


As a CPU Logic Design Engineer, you will play a key role in shaping future CPU designs, working closely with architects and cross-functional teams from feature definition through silicon delivery. This position offers significant technical ownership and the opportunity to influence both microarchitectural definition and RTL implementation of key CPU features.

Responsibilities

  • Define and implement architecture and microarchitecture features for next-generation CPU cores.
  • Own the logic design of complex, performance-critical CPU blocks from specification through integration.
  • Develop high-quality RTL and drive optimizations for power, performance, area, and timing (PPA) goals.
  • Analyze architectural tradeoffs and contribute to microarchitectural decisions.
  • Lead technical discussions and design reviews across multiple engineering disciplines.
  • Collaborate closely with architecture, verification, performance, physical design, and validation teams throughout the development cycle.
  • Debug complex pre-silicon and post-silicon issues and drive root-cause analysis to closure.

What You'll Work On

  • High-IPC CPU pipeline development and optimization.
  • Instruction fetch, decode, scheduling, execution, and retirement logic.
  • Advanced power, frequency, and performance optimization techniques.
  • Next-generation CPU features targeting client, server, cloud, and AI workloads.
  • Some of the largest and most sophisticated RTL designs in the industry.

Impact

Your work will directly influence the architecture, microarchitecture, and implementation of future Intel CPU cores. You will help solve some of the industry's most challenging design problems while contributing to products that power computing at global scale.

This role offers substantial ownership, broad architectural exposure, and the opportunity to drive features from early definition through silicon execution.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualification

  • Bachelor's or BS degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of experience in CPU logic design.
  • Proven expertise in RTL coding and simulation for CPU designs.
  • Strong knowledge of CPU architecture and microarchitecture features.
  • Experience with logic optimization for power, performance, area, and timing metrics.
  • Proficiency in hardware description languages such as Verilog or VHDL.
  • Familiarity with design verification tools and methodologies
  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical initiatives and drive execution.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working on high-performance CPU designs in advanced technology nodes.
  • Strong understanding of physical design and its impact on logic implementation.
  • Proven track record of mentoring technical leaders and fostering team development.
  • Ability to align technical strategy with business objectives to achieve organizational goals.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with a history of influencing technical direction across teams and industries.

title: Senior Technical Sales Architect, AI Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel is looking for a senior technologist who pairs deep silicon and systems knowledge with sound business judgment to lead AI infrastructure sales cycles in Asia Pacific and Japan. You will partner with cloud service providers and soverign AI model builders to design, benchmark and scale Intel-based AI infrastructure, from memory subsystem to the rack to the power budget, including agentic AI platforms. You are the technical lead in the deal, accountable for the architecture, the evidence and the outcome.

What You'll Do

  • Technical discovery: Lead architecture workshops with CTOs, platform and AI engineering teams, mapping workloads, SLAs, power and facility limits to business outcomes.
  • Architecture and design: Architect end-to-end AI infrastructure on Intel Xeon (AMX), Intel accelerators and memory (DDR5, MRDIMM, HBM, CXL), including disaggregated compute, memory and storage, prefill/decode separation, kv offload and rack-scale networking.
  • Rack to power to sustainability: Size racks, cooling (air and liquid), PUE and performance per watt, and build the TCO and carbon case for power-constrained data centers.
  • Benchmarks and PoCs: Design and lead reproducible benchmarks and PoCs (LLM serving, RAG, agentic workloads) with agreed acceptance criteria, measuring tokens per second, time to first token, cost per task and performance per watt against competing platforms.
  • Agentic transformation: Define reference architectures maximizing Intel goodness for agent platforms: CPU orchestration, long-context memory, sandboxes, tool and data connectors (MCP), vector databases, observability, security and data residency.
  • Pursuit leadership: Partner with account managers on proposals, SoWs, RFP/RFI responses and executive briefings, in Korean and English.
  • Ecosystem: Work with OEMs , SIs, memory vendors and software partners to deliver validated, supportable solutions.
  • Roadmap feedback: Turn field evidence into requirements for Intel product management and engineering.

Qualifications:

You must meet the qualifications below to be considered. Experience may come from degree, research, or prior roles and internships.


  • Education: Bachelor's in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Experience: 8+ years in customer-facing solutions architecture, technical sales or presales for data center compute, memory or AI infrastructure.
  • Platform depth: Server architecture (CPU, memory hierarchy, PCIe, CXL, networking, storage) and how it drives AI performance.
  • AI software: PyTorch and an LLM serving framework such as vLLM; the performance profile of inference and training; RAG and agent frameworks.
  • Infrastructure: Data center networking (Ethernet, RoCE, InfiniBand), containers and Kubernetes, rack power and cooling fundamentals.
  • Benchmarking: Proven record of running reproducible benchmarks and PoCs and defending the results to customer engineers.
  • Supply chain and ODM: Working knowledge of ODM and OEM design and manufacturing models, OCP-style rack integration, and how to work with Taiwan-based partners across time zones.
  • Communication: Ability to turn multi-node cluster designs into business outcomes for executives; business fluency in Korean and English.

Preferred Qualifications


  • These are in addition to the minimum qualifications and are a plus when identifying top candidates.
  • Track record with CSPs. CoSPs and their procurement structures.
  • Hands-on with Intel Xeon (AMX), Gaudi or Intel GPUs, or competing GPU platforms; OpenVINO and oneAPI.
  • Existing relationships with ODMs and system makersand experience taking ODM designs to enterprise or hyperscale buyers; .
  • Depth in disaggregation: CXL pooling and tiering, composable infrastructure, OCP racks, liquid cooling.
  • Large-scale inference economics: cost per million tokens, tokens per second per watt, fleet capacity planning.
  • Agentic AI: LangGraph or Semantic Kernel, MCP, vector databases, agent evaluation; has advised an enterprise agentic program.
  • Data center sustainability metrics: PUE, carbon intensity, power capping.
  • Influence over senior engineering and product leaders without direct authority; MBA or equivalent.

title: Physical Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

  • Performs physical design implementation of custom IP and SoC designs from RTL to GDS to create a design database that is ready for manufacturing.
  • Conducts all aspects of the physical design flow including synthesis, place and route, clock tree synthesis, floor planning, static timing analysis, power/clock distribution, reliability, and power and noise analysis.
  • Conducts verification and signoff including formal equivalence verification, static timing analysis, reliability verification, static and dynamic power integrity, layout verification, electrical rule checking, and structural design checking.
  • Analyzes results and makes recommendations to fix violations for current and future product architecture.
  • Possesses expertise in various aspects of structural and physical design, including physical clock design, timing closure, coverage analysis, multiple power domain analysis, placing, routing, synthesis, and DFT using industry standard EDA tools.
  • Optimizes design to improve productlevel parameters such as power, frequency, and area.
  • Participates in the development and improvement of physical design methodologies and flow automation.

Qualifications:

  • You should possess a relevant educational qualification, BSEE or equivalent with 10+ years / MSEE or equivalent with 8+ years of design experience in the structural/physical design domain.

Additional qualifications include:

  • Experience in multiple tape-outs and timing closure for deep sub-micron, multi-GHz designs.
  • Extensive hands-on expertise in STA and timing signoff, including SDC development, timing budgeting, constraint validation, and PrimeTime/PrimeTime SI.
  • Strong STA methodology knowledge, including MCMM, PVT/extraction corners, POCV/AOCV/LVF, timing margining, and guard-banding.
  • Extensive knowledge of EDA and RTL-to-GDS flows, including synthesis, floorplanning, place-and-route, CTS, and low-power/multi-power domain design.

title: Senior Linux I/O and Sensor Integration Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
We are seeking a Senior Linux I/O and Sensor Integration Engineer to connect humanoid robot hardware to a Linux/x86 and ROS 2 software platform. You will own non-camera sensor and peripheral enablement, from Linux drivers and transport interfaces to reliable, timestamped data delivery. Your work will provide the observable, maintainable hardware interfaces required by robotics perception, state estimation, and control teams.

Key Responsibilities

  • Bring up and integrate robot peripherals and sensors over interfaces such as I2C, SPI, UART, GPIO, USB, PCIe, CAN/CAN FD, and EtherCAT, based on the platform design.
  • Develop, adapt, and debug Linux kernel drivers and user-space interfaces for devices such as IMUs, joint encoders, force/torque sensors, tactile sensors, and LiDAR units.
  • Use standard Linux interfaces such as IIO, SocketCAN, spidev, and serial interfaces where appropriate, selecting maintainable kernel or user-space integration paths for each device.
  • Develop ROS 2 device nodes and hardware adapters with appropriate message types, frame identifiers, QoS settings, lifecycle behavior, configuration, and diagnostics.
  • Implement and validate sensor timestamping, clock-domain conversion, hardware triggers, and synchronization mechanisms where supported; characterize acquisition-to-publication latency and jitter.
  • Diagnose electrical, protocol, driver, and middleware failures using schematics, datasheets, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, bus captures, and software traces.
  • Implement error detection, timeout handling, reconnection, and recovery; expose device health, packet loss, stale data, and communication errors to the robotics stack.
  • Build hardware-in-the-loop and endurance tests covering data integrity, sustained rates, disconnection, recovery, and concurrent operation with camera and GPU workloads.
  • Collaborate with hardware and robotics teams on interface requirements, calibration-data handling, and maintainable integration documentation.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 7+ years of relevant software engineering experience in Linux device drivers, embedded systems, robotics hardware integration, or related development.
  • Hands-on experience integrating physical sensors or peripherals on Linux/x86, including board-level bring-up and hardware/software troubleshooting.
  • Strong C/C++ skills and proficiency in Python or shell scripting for diagnostics and test automation.
  • Practical depth in multiple device interfaces, including at least one board-level bus, such as I2C or SPI, and one external transport, such as CAN, USB, or Ethernet.
  • Experience developing or integrating ROS 2 device interfaces on physical robotic systems, including practical understanding of message timestamps, coordinate frames, and QoS.
  • Ability to read schematics and component datasheets and use laboratory instruments to isolate hardware and protocol problems.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with humanoid robots, mobile manipulators, dexterous hands, or other multi-sensor robotic platforms.
  • Experience with Linux IO drivers, SocketCAN/CANopen, or ros2_control hardware interfaces.
  • Familiarity with PTP, hardware timestamping, trigger distribution, and multi-sensor clock synchronization.
  • Experience supporting sensor calibration workflows, validating measurements, or diagnosing data-quality issues with state-estimation teams.
  • Experience coordinating with microcontroller firmware developers and validating host-to-device protocol compatibility.
  • Experience designing automated fault-injection tests and long-duration reliability monitoring for deployed hardware.

title: Sr. Manager, Intel vPro Enterprise Deployments
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel is shaping the future of technology to help create a better future for the entire world. Our work in pushing forward fields like AI, analytics, and cloud-to-edge technology is at the heart of countless innovations. With a career at Intel, you'll have the opportunity to use technology to power major breakthroughs and create enhancements that improve our everyday quality of life. Join us and help make the future more wonderful for everyone. Want to learn more? Visit our YouTube Channel or the link below.

Life at Intel


Intel vPro is the platform enterprises rely on to secure, manage, and scale their PC fleets. Adoption is growing, and the market is changing quickly. Organizations are moving agentic AI workloads from experimentation onto the client PC, and they need those workloads to run inside the management, security, and compliance controls they already operate.

Customer interest is strong. What determines success is technical execution: getting from evaluation to production through real-world enterprise networks, identity systems, security reviews, and device images. This role exists to close that gap. You will be the technical lead who takes prioritized enterprise customers and lighthouse pilots to production, and who turns what you learn in the field into product and engineering improvements.

You will work directly with customer IT architects, security teams, and executives, and with Intel product, engineering, and customer success teams. Your work will shape how enterprises deploy agentic client computing at scale and how Intel vPro supports it.

Responsibilities:

  • Enterprise Customer Technical Engagement
  • Technical lead: Own the technical side of prioritized enterprise accounts from evaluation through production activation across Intel vPro manageability, security, and cloud-based fleet services.
  • Discovery: Run structured technical discovery covering networking endpoint management, OEM mix.
  • Deployment architecture: Define the activation plan, including provisioning mode, wired and Wi-Fi profiles, and migration paths from on-premises to cloud-based management.
  • Blocker removal: Clear deployment obstacles such as security questionnaires and infosec reviews, network policy changes, and OEM image or driver issues.
  • Customer presence: Provide technical leadership in customer executive meetings, on-site workshops, and architecture reviews.
  • Clean handoff: Transition accounts to steady-state support with a documented environment profile.
  • Agentic Client Deployment in the Managed Enterprise
  • Help customers move agentic workloads on client PCs from experimentation to governed, supportable fleet deployment.
  • Readiness and architecture: Assess fleet readiness (platform generation, NPU/GPU capability, memory and storage headroom, vPro enablement, OS and driver baselines) and define customer reference architectures covering device tiers, local model and runtime stack, identity, network, management plane, and security controls.
  • Workload placement: Help customers decide which agentic workloads run locally, in the cloud, or in a hybrid split based on data sensitivity, latency, cost, and device capability, using device telemetry to inform routing decisions.
  • Provisioning and lifecycle: Design zero-touch provisioning for agentic-ready devices, define golden images and driver baselines for AI workloads, and establish how local models and agent runtimes are packaged, distributed, versioned, and rolled back through existing software distribution tools.
  • Staged rollout: Set up rollout rings (anchor customer and pilot, early adopters, broad deployment) with clear gates between rings.
  • Security and governance: Map deployments to the customer's security baseline, including hardware root of trust, TPM-backed credentials, BitLocker, Secured-core and VBS settings, and vPro hardware-based threat detection. Work with security teams on agent identity, least-privilege access, and data protection for prompts, outputs, and agent logs.
  • Containment and recovery: Define response for agent misbehavior or compromise, including device isolation, remote wipe or reimage, and out-of-band recovery when the OS is unresponsive.
  • Day-2 operations: Define monitoring for performance, thermals, battery impact, NPU/GPU utilization, and agent health; build help desk runbooks; set power and performance baselines; and advise on device tiers and refresh planning.
  • Lighthouse Customer Engagements
  • Pilot ownership: Lead technical execution of lighthouse pilots for agentic client computers built on Intel vPro.
  • Success criteria: Define measurable pilot criteria with customers and internal teams, covering business outcomes, security sign-off, and fleet operability.
  • White glove support: Provide hands-on support to early customers, including device preparation, provisioning, configuration tuning, and issue triage with a direct path to engineering.
  • Device and software hygiene: Ensure pilot devices ship clean, with images and drivers that match the commercial baseline.
  • Pilot exit: Track pilot stage, confidence, and blockers, and run exit readouts with a clear go/no-go recommendation for production rollout.
  • Proof points: Capture measured outcomes and turn them into proof points and case-study inputs.
  • Anchor Customer Program and Product Feedback
  • Anchor customers: Serve as technical liaison to anchor enterprise customers who adopt new capabilities first and validate pre-release features in their environments before broader lighthouse rollout.
  • Blocker tracking: Track anchor customer adoption blockers to closure with product owners.
  • Engineering inputs: Turn field findings into actionable engineering inputs, including issue reports with reproduction data, change requests backed by business-impact data, and product requirements.
  • Quality loop: Feed real customer issues into validation so the same issue does not reach the next customer, and close the loop with customers and the field through release notes and best known methods.
  • Scale and Enablement
  • Convert engagement and pilot learnings into reusable assets: deployment playbooks, reference architectures, best known methods, and pilot kits.
  • Enable regional technical sales teams to repeat proven deployment patterns independently.
  • Contribute to technical white papers for customer and partner audiences.

Who You Will Work With:
Customer IT, security, and network architects; customer executives; Intel customer success, product management, platform and firmware engineering, validation, and regional technical sales teams; and OEM and software ecosystem partners where they are part of the customer's architecture.

What Success Looks Like:


  • Lighthouse pilots that convert to production deployments, with shorter time from pilot start to activation.
  • Agentic-ready devices deployed under customer management and passing customer security reviews.
  • Deployment blockers resolved and devices activated on engaged accounts.
  • Field findings accepted into the product roadmap, and repeat issues prevented through validation.
  • Published reference architectures and playbooks that regional teams use independently.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience listed below would be obtained through a combination of your school work/classes/research and/or relevant previous job and/or internship experiences.


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.
  • 10+ years of experience in enterprise endpoint, client platform, or solutions engineering roles, including customer-facing technical leadership.
  • Hands-on experience deploying and managing enterprise PC fleets within an agentic environment.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Working knowledge of enterprise networking and identity: 802.1X, EAP-TLS, RADIUS, PKI (AD CS, NDES, SCEP), Entra ID, and Active Directory.
  • Experience with enterprise endpoint security: TPM, BitLocker, Secured-core PC, VBS, EDR, and DLP.
  • Scripting proficiency in PowerShell.
  • Deep knowledge of Intel vPro and Intel Active Management Technology (AMT), including provisioning, remote access, KVM, and out-of-band management.
  • Hands-on experience with AI PC and agentic software stacks: local model runtimes, NPU/GPU drivers, agent frameworks, and hybrid local-cloud execution.
  • Experience designing least-privilege access models and governance for AI workloads on endpoints.

title: Senior Linux BSP Integration Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

We are seeking a Senior Linux BSP Integration Engineer to build and maintain the Linux platform foundation for humanoid robots powered by Intel x86 processors. You will own board support package integration, platform bring-up, and release readiness and ROS 2 software to operate reliably as one system. This is a hands-on systems engineering role spanning hardware, firmware, the Linux kernel, and user space.

Key Responsibilities

  • Bring up Intel x86 compute boards and integrate Linux kernels, platform firmware dependencies, device drivers, root filesystems, and system services into reproducible BSP releases.
  • Diagnose platform issues across UEFI/BIOS handoff, ACPI device enumeration, PCIe, interrupts, DMA, IOMMU configuration, and power management in collaboration with hardware and firmware teams.
  • Integrate subsystem software delivered by subsystem owners; resolve kernel, firmware, library, and package compatibility issues across the platform.
  • Establish the OS environment for ROS 2 deployment, including device permissions, persistent device naming, service startup ordering, networking, and container access to hardware.
  • Investigate boot failures, kernel crashes, memory corruption, device enumeration failures, resource contention, and suspend/resume issues using system traces and reproducible test cases.
  • Characterize boot time, CPU and memory utilization, I/O throughput, power consumption, and thermal behavior under representative robot workloads; implement and validate platform-level improvements.
  • Build automated hardware-based regression and endurance tests, maintain supported software configurations, and deliver release notes, integration guides, and actionable defect reports.
  • Drive cross-functional issue resolution with board vendors, firmware engineers, subsystem developers, and robotics software teams from prototype bring-up through deployment.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 10+ years of relevant software engineering experience, including hands-on Linux BSP integration, embedded Linux development, or platform bring-up.
  • Practical experience bringing up and debugging Linux on x86 hardware, with knowledge of the Linux boot flow, kernel configuration, loadable modules, device enumeration, and system services.
  • Proficiency in C/C++ and Python or shell scripting, with experience using Git, build systems, and automated testing.
  • Demonstrated ability to isolate failures across hardware, firmware, kernel, and user-space boundaries using tools such as GDB, crash dumps, ftrace, perf, and kernel logs.
  • Experience integrating multiple hardware subsystems into a working platform and validating their operation under concurrent workloads.
  • Ability to communicate technical findings clearly and independently drive complex integration issues to closure.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience deploying Linux platforms on physical robots, autonomous machines, or other sensor-rich edge systems; humanoid robot experience is especially relevant.
  • Familiarity with ROS 2 deployment, DDS networking, and debugging hardware-dependent robotics software.
  • Experience with Yocto Project/OpenEmbedded or reproducible Debian/Ubuntu image and package pipelines.
  • Experience with Intel platform power management, GPU software dependencies, thermal analysis, or PCIe reliability debugging.
  • Experience with hardware-in-the-loop testing, BSP lifecycle maintenance, upstream contributions, or coordination with open-source maintainers.

title: Senior STA Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As a Physical Design Timing Engineer, you will play a critical role in ensuring the success of complex System-on-Chip (SoC) designs through advanced timing analysis and optimization techniques. You will focus on timing closure, constraint development, and clock network design to deliver high-performance, low-power solutions. This position offers the opportunity to collaborate across multidisciplinary teams and contribute to cutting-edge technology developments that shape the future of computing.

Business Group
Join Intel's Devices Development Group, a highly regarded organization responsible for creating innovative Client SoCs for next-generation laptop and desktop computers. Our team specializes in driving forward-thinking designs and delivering performance-optimized solutions. Focused on advancing Intel's leadership in computing, we work on groundbreaking projects that push the boundaries of technology while fostering a collaborative and dynamic environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Conduct timing analysis and timing closure across Multi-Mode and Multi-Corner Multi-Voltage domain designs at chip, block, and subsystem levels.
  • Define and develop methodologies to ensure high-quality timing models that enable streamlined physical design workflows.
  • Generate, verify, and optimize timing constraints while resolving timing violations efficiently.
  • Define process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) conditions to ensure designs align with product plans and operating conditions.
  • Collaborate with architecture, clocking design, and logic design teams to validate high-performance, low-power clock network guidelines.
  • Lead timing ECO implementation strategies and enable automation flows using STA tools.
  • Develop scripts for methodology optimization within industry-accepted tools such as Synopsys or Cadence.
  • Work on LVF/POCV variation formats and address deep sub-micron design challenges.
  • Act as a liaison between timing analysis and physical design teams, ensuring project alignment and high-quality deliverables.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Electronics, VLSI, Computer Science, or a related field with 7+ years of hands-on experience in timing analysis and optimization OR Master's degree in Electronics, VLSI, Computer Science, or a related field with 6+ years of relevant experience OR PhD in a relevant field with no prior professional experience.
  • Proficiency in STA tools such as Tweaker/Prime Time and ECO implementation strategies.
  • Experience in RTL-to-GDSII digital design implementation using tools from Synopsys or Cadence.
  • Familiarity with LVF/POCV variation formats and understanding of sub-micron design principles.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop automation scripts using Python, Perl, or TCL.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Deep expertise in timing analysis methodologies for complex SoC designs.
  • Experience with constraint generation, development, and cleanup.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

title: Advanced Packaging Failure Analysis Engineer – Federal
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact

Low Yield Analysis (LYA) engineers are responsible for end-of-line failure analysis of the assembly and substrate process and identifying key mechanisms that contribute to ultimate root cause identification. This can relate to specific electrical failures and/or be driven via understanding in-line defect and process health (for Defect Characterization LYA). Engineers will be expected to conduct hands on lab work, define data acquisition strategies, data analysis plans, and recommend corrective actions/fixes to internal customers. The LYA engineer will utilize strong presentation skills to influence individual process engineers as well as platform teams. Analysis will include both electrical fault isolation (FI) and physical failure analysis (FA) collection. The LYA engineer will also interact with a large team of technicians and engineers to provide guidance and mentoring on a wide variety of FI/FA methods and strategies. Other duties may include process and defect characterization and developing innovative techniques/approaches to accelerate failure identification and root cause mechanism understanding. LYA engineers will be expected to provide consultation concerning packaging/assembly challenges and work with partner organizations towards improvements in the manufacturing process. The ability to rapidly respond to customer/client requests or events as they occur while developing solutions utilizing formal education and engineering judgment will be anticipated.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead end-to-end investigations to identify and resolve complex yield, defect, and quality issues.
  • Support equipment installation and start-up of advanced analytical equipment.
  • Serve as a technical owner for major factory, platform, or technology development programs.
  • Define characterization strategies, learning plans, and root cause methodologies for critical technical challenges.
  • Utilize advanced analytical techniques including Optical Microscopy, SEM/EDS, EBSD, CSAM, FTIR, Raman, FIB, ion milling, and mechanical cross-sectioning to identify failure mechanisms.
  • Utilize advanced fault isolation techniques including curve tracing, electrical hand proving, EBIC, IBIC, TIVA, LIVA, EOTPR, SQUID, SSM, ELITE
  • Correlate characterization results with electrical data, defect inspection data, process history, and manufacturing information to establish root cause.
  • Consolidate and analyze large data sets using statistical methods and coding tools to identify yield limiters and emerging trends.
  • Develop and implement tools, dashboards, automation, and analytical methodologies that improve learning velocity and analysis efficiency.
  • Drive corrective actions and influence process improvements across manufacturing, integration, quality, and technology organizations.
  • Lead cross-functional task forces and technical reviews to address high-priority yield and reliability issues.
  • Present technical findings, recommendations, and risk assessments to engineering and management teams.
  • Mentor engineers and technicians while promoting best-known methods and organizational learning.
  • Support future capability development through equipment strategy, methodology development, and characterization roadmap planning.
  • Effectively manage multiple high-priority investigations while balancing customer commitments, factory priorities, and business needs.

#cj

  • Enable pre-silicon and post-silicon validation, including shift-left and virtual-platform validation.

title: Semiconductor Device Modeling PhD Intern
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

At Intel, we are shaping the future of technology. From enabling AI and cloud computing to powering next-generation semiconductor innovations, Intel engineers solve some of the world's most complex challenges. Join us and help build technology that improves the lives of billions of people around the globe. 

 The Compact Device Modeling Group (CDMG) within Intel's Design Technology Platform Organization is seeking a highly motivated Semiconductor Device Modeling Intern to characterize semiconductor device behavior and develop, update, and validate compact models for emerging process technologies, while ensuring reliable and accurate simulation results.  

In this role, you will develop and validate industry-standard (or equivalent) compact models (BSIM-CMG) for advanced CMOS technologies, and build the software tooling that makes model extraction, verification, and deployment faster and more reliable. The work sits at the intersection of semiconductor device physics, analytical and numerical methods, and software engineering, and feeds directly into PDK releases used by circuit designers. 

Responsibilities 

  • Validate model behavior across DC, CV, temperature, and geometry scaling; investigate discrepancies and propose fixes. 
  • Develop and maintain internal automation tools for extraction flows, regression testing and model QA. 
  • Run SPICE simulations and build automated benchmark and quality assurance suites.  
  • Gain hands-on training in advanced transistor technologies, including FinFET and future technology architectures. 
  • Collaborate with technology development and design engineering leadership to shape the direction of circuit tools, compact modeling methodologies, and process file development. 
  • Contribute to documentation of tools and their usage along with technical findings.  
  • Communicate progress, challenges, and recommendations effectively to team members and stakeholders. 

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications 

  • Pursuing a PhD degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics, Materials Science, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline with 3+ months of relevant experience through internships, research, academic projects, or coursework 
  • Minimum GPA of 3.0.  
  • Understanding of semiconductor device fundamentals and electrical characterization concepts. 
  • Experience with at least one programming or scripting language such as Python, C or C++, MATLAB. 
  • Familiarity with Unix/Linux environments.  

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Coursework or research experience in semiconductor device physics and transistor operation, and software development. 
  • Familiarity with FinFET, CMOS technology, or advanced semiconductor process technologies. 
  • Experience with electrical characterization techniques, including DC, CV, and RF measurements. 
  • Knowledge of semiconductor device modeling concepts and parameter extraction methodologies. 
  • Proficiency in Python; comfortable with version control (Git) and scripting on Linux. 
  • Familiarity with SPICE-class circuit simulation and netlist construction.  
  • Experience through academic research, laboratory projects, internships, or published technical work related to semiconductor technologies.

title: Senior AI Algorithms & GPU Performance Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Business Group
You will join Intel's Data Center Group, working on high-performance AI and data center computing. Our team combines advanced algorithms, GPU optimization, and performance engineering to maximize the efficiency of modern AI and LLM workloads.


As a Senior AI Algorithms & GPU Performance Engineer at Intel, you will join a highly skilled team developing extremely high-performance GPU kernels for modern AI and LLM workloads, including those used by inference engines such as SGLang and vLLM.


You will analyze AI operators, identify performance bottlenecks, and develop optimized algorithms and GPU kernels. We are looking for engineers who can reason deeply about algorithms, GPU architecture, parallelism, data movement, and numerical computation to solve complex performance challenges.

Your work will directly improve the performance and efficiency of AI workloads on Intel GPU platforms.



Key Responsibilities:

  • Design and optimize high-performance GPU kernels and algorithms for modern AI workloads.
  • Develop efficient computational approaches that leverage GPU architecture, parallelism, and memory hierarchy.
  • Optimize critical AI operations, including matrix and attention-related computations and other compute-intensive and memory-intensive primitives.
  • Profile and benchmark workloads to identify bottlenecks and drive optimization through quantitative performance analysis.
  • Collaborate across AI, compiler, architecture, and software teams to deliver high-impact technical solutions.

Why Join Us
Join a friendly, collaborative team at the leading edge of Intel's AI development, solving challenging problems where innovative algorithms and GPU optimization directly impact AI performance.

We value technical excellence, creativity, teamwork, and knowledge sharing, with a hybrid work model including one day per week working from home.

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, or a related technical field.
  • 5+ years of relevant industry experience in high-performance computing, AI, algorithms, or performance optimization.
  • Strong programming skills in C++ and experience with parallel programming. Python experience is an advantage.
  • Strong understanding of algorithms, numerical computation, and computer architecture, with demonstrated ability to apply them to creative solutions for complex performance problems.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze computational workloads, identify performance bottlenecks, and develop efficient solutions.
  • Experience optimizing performance using GPU, SIMD, DSP, or other parallel and vector processing architectures.

  • Hands-on experience developing or optimizing high-performance kernels for AI, machine learning, signal processing, or high-performance computing workloads.

  • Experience with AI workloads such as matrix operations, attention, LLM inference, or related numerical primitives.

title: Module Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Job Description: Join Intel and build a better tomorrow. Intel is undergoing an exciting transformation, with a vision to create and extend computing technology to connect and enrich the lives of every person on Earth. Join us and help create the next generation of technologies that will shape the future for decades to come. The Intel Foundry Technology Development (TD) team is seeking an experienced Senior Lithography Module Development Engineer to drive the development, optimization, and manufacturing readiness of advanced lithography processes for next-generation mask making technologies. TD Lithography Module Development Engineers are responsible for the development and execution of current and next-generation lithography manufacturing processes. They enable the manufacture of innovative device architectures, demonstrate the manufacturing viability of complex novel processes, and support high-volume manufacturing (HVM) operations. In this senior technical role, you will provide leadership in advanced patterning technologies, lithography process and equipment development, defect reduction, and yield improvement. You will collaborate across engineering disciplines and with equipment and materials suppliers to advance lithography capabilities and enable successful technology development and manufacturing ramps. Key Responsibilities: Responsibilities will include, but are not limited to: • Lead the design and execution of complex experiments, process characterization, and data analysis to develop and optimize EUV and DUV lithography processes that meet critical dimension, overlay, defectivity, yield, and manufacturing requirements. • Partner with equipment suppliers and internal engineering teams to develop, characterize, qualify, and improve advanced lithography equipment and process capabilities. Identify equipment limitations, drive hardware and process improvements, and establish robust manufacturing solutions. • Collaborate with process integration, etch, thin films, metrology, and yield engineering teams to develop novel patterning solutions, resolve complex process interactions, and improve device performance and yield. • Lead systematic root cause investigations and corrective actions for lithography-related process and equipment excursions. Develop strategies to improve process stability, reduce defectivity, and enhance manufacturing performance. • Collaborate with photomask, reticle, and scanner engineering teams to optimize imaging performance, reticle quality, defect management, and advanced patterning capabilities. • Lead the qualification and ramp of advanced lithography processes and equipment at the TD site. Support the transfer of technology to Intel manufacturing facilities through Copy Exactly methodology, ensuring consistent process performance and equipment matching across sites. • Provide technical direction and mentorship to engineers, lead cross-functional problem-solving efforts, and communicate technical findings and recommendations to engineering leadership. Collaborate with external technology partners to advance next-generation lithography capabilities. • Drive the development of intellectual property, new process methodologies, and innovative solutions that enable future semiconductor technology nodes while improving process capability, cost, and manufacturing efficiency.

Qualifications:

 You must possess the following minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.
Minimum Qualifications:
• Master's degree or PhD in Physics, Chemistry, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Optics, or related science or engineering discipline.
• Minimum of 8 years of experience in:

- Relevant semiconductor process development, equipment engineering, or advanced manufacturing experience with a Master's degree, or equivalent relevant experience with a PhD.
• Designing and executing experiments, analyzing complex engineering data, and applying statistical methods to process development, optimization, and troubleshooting.
• Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical investigations, resolve manufacturing or process challenges, and collaborate effectively across engineering disciplines.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience in semiconductor lithography, advanced patterning, or closely related semiconductor process technologies.
• Extensive hands-on experience with advanced EUV and/or DUV lithography processes, including scanner systems, track equipment, photoresist processes, masks, and associated metrology.
• Strong understanding of lithography process fundamentals, including imaging performance, critical dimension control, overlay, process windows, defectivity, and process stability.
• Experience with photomask and reticle technologies, including mask qualification, inspection, reticle defect management, and scanner-reticle interactions.
• Demonstrated experience with lithography process and equipment development, qualification, yield improvement, and high-volume manufacturing ramp.
• Proficiency with statistical process control (SPC), design of experiments (DOE), and advanced data analysis tools such as JMP, Python, MATLAB, or equivalent platforms.
• Experience applying machine learning, artificial intelligence, or advanced analytics to semiconductor process optimization, equipment performance, or defect reduction.
• Experience working directly with semiconductor equipment or materials suppliers to develop and implement new technologies and resolve complex technical challenges.
• Demonstrated technical leadership, including mentoring engineers, leading cross-functional initiatives, and communicating complex technical findings to senior engineering leadership.

Job Details:

Job Description: 

Organization Overview:
Manufacturing Development Customer Engineering (MDCE) is Intel's newest organization within Intel Foundry Technology Manufacturing (FTM). We bridge the critical gap between Technology Development (TD) and High-Volume Manufacturing (HVM), advancing technology nodes and process capability from initial product qualification to high-yield production across multiple products while enhancing technologies for our foundry customers.

About This Role:
Join Intel's Manufacturing Development and Customer Engineering (MDCE) team as a Staff Engineer driving process innovation across Intel's most advanced semiconductor technologies in volume manufacturing. You will spearhead the development, optimization, and manufacturability of critical thin film deposition processes, ensuring seamless transitions from early development to high-volume production while meeting Intel foundry customer requirements.

Your Mission:
Lead thin film process excellence across epitaxy, anneal, implant, CVD, ALD, thermal/plasma deposition, and/or treatment technologies. Operating at the nexus of Technology Development and High-Volume Manufacturing, you will drive breakthrough solutions for Intel 18A, Intel 3, 12nm, and next-generation technology nodes.

Process Innovation and Excellence

title: Linux Graphics Virtualization (SR-IOV) Intern
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the team You will join the Linux Graphics Virtualization team. We enable SR-IOV on Intel GPUs for client and server platforms. descriptionHtml:

As a Senior STA Signoff Engineer, you will play a critical role in delivering high-performance, low-power custom IP and SoC designs, enabling Intel's cutting-edge technological advancements. Your responsibilities will include but not limited to leading and executing Fullchip/subsystem Static Timing analysis and Signoff, Design convergence to meet the PPA targets, Tape-out audits, Constraints development and management, timing correlation against silicon learnings . - Perform STA analysis and timing/leakage ECO Convergence cycles for subsystem/Fullchip for the SOC designs.
- Execute timing analysis, power distribution optimization, and noise glitch/signal integrity analysis to meet design specifications.
- Analyze design results, identify violations, and recommend fixes to improve physical design convergence.
- Optimize timing, clock tree, and other design aspects to enhance power, frequency, and area parameters.
- Collaborate with PD teams to drive signoff closure for tapeout and meet IP technical and delivery requirements.

The successful candidate will contribute to the development and optimization of security data planes and AI-enabled security workloads. title: Silicon Packaging Architect
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Role Overview:

The Silicon Packaging Architect (Test Chips) is the pivotal technical owner driving the architectural definition, substrate pathfinding, and co-design of advanced package solutions for silicon validation vehicles, IP test chips (Serdes, HSIO, PCIE, LPDDR, DDR, UCIE-S, UCIE-A, Foundational IPs), and technology demonstration platforms. This role sits at the critical intersection of Silicon IP, Package Design, and Post-Silicon Validation. You will be responsible for defining the packaging architecture of test chips, translating complex IP validation requirements into physical package implementations and board-level interfaces to ensure seamless hardware bring-up and technology certification.

Organization Overview:

You will be part of the Hard IP Development (HIPD) Test Chip Development (TCD) team, an integral part of Intel’s Central Engineering Group (CEG). Our charter is to provide end-to-end Test Chip solutions that enable IP technology validation and risk reduction across differentiated technologies, including Memory, HSIO, PCIe, SerDes, UCIe-A/S, and Foundation IPs. Our validation capabilities and platforms cover both PHY and complex subsystems. We also partner with IP teams to enable validation of next-generation I/O technologies.   

Role & Responsibilities:

  • Lead Test Chip Package Architecture: Lead the definition, trade-off analysis, and technical roadmap for test vehicle packaging platforms. Translate IP/product requirements into package architecture specifications. Evaluate standard flip-chip BGA and advanced 2.5D/3D packaging options to align with IP and test chip objectives. Lead technology trade-off decisions considering electrical, performance and reusability.
  • Drive End-to-End Package Solution: Leads the full package development process, from definition through design and execution to ensure silicon packages conform to electrical, mechanical, thermal, and reliability standards, specifications, and landing zones. Collaborates with silicon team, package assembly team, board teams (EV, TIU), hardware, and package teams to deliver high-quality packages meeting committed timely and quality.
  • Silicon-Package-Board Co-Optimization: Drive the co-design of silicon floorplans, bump patterns, and ball-map definitions. Balance constraints across silicon physical design, high-density package substrate routing, and system board layout.
  • Milestone Reviews & Checklist Ownership: Establish and maintain rigorous package-level co-design milestone checklists. Act as the gatekeeper for design reviews (Concept, SI/PI Sign-off, and Tape-out approval) to guarantee execution quality.
  • IP Integration & Requirements Gathering: Partner directly with front-end silicon and IP development teams to gather physical requirements, capabilities, and electrical specifications for incoming IP blocks.
  • Interface Co-Design & SI/PI Alignment: Drive architectural layout decisions for high-speed test interfaces (e.g., PCIe, UCIe D2D links, LPDDR, DDR, HSIO, SerDes). Collaborate with simulation teams to meet strict channel budgets and power delivery network (PDN) target impedance.Liaise with Full-Custom and SI/PI teams on package simulations to meet overall electrical, power, and signal performance specifications.
  • Board-Level Integration & PCB Layout Trials: Collaborate with system-hardware teams on product PCB layout trials. Ensure the test platform boards accommodate the test chip’s routing, power, and diagnostic requirements.
  • Test Vehicle Execution & Technology Certification: Manage project milestones, delivery schedules, and stakeholder alignment to execute layouts successfully, taking the test vehicle package from planning to tape-out.
  • Post-Silicon Bring-up & Validation Strategy: Partner with post-silicon validation teams to develop testing strategies for both High Volume Manufacturing (HVM) and bench-level testing, actively participating in lab bring-up, debug, and failure analysis (FA).

What You Should Bring to the Role

To be successful in this position, you should demonstrate the following professional traits:

  • A collaborative mindset with the ability to align cross-functional stakeholders across silicon, package, board, and validation teams
  • Strong ownership and accountability in driving complex, multi-disciplinary projects from definition to tape-out
  • Clear and effective communication when translating technical requirements across engineering disciplines, and the ability to present complex layout data as clear decisions for senior leaders

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, Materials Science, or Physics with 10+ years of industry experience
  • OR Bachelor's degree with 12+ years of industry experience
  • 8+ years of dedicated experience in semiconductor packaging or test chip board design
  • Understanding of high-speed serial/parallel interfaces (PCIe Gen5/6, high-speed SerDes, UCIe die-to-die links) and memory subsystems (DDR4/DDR5/LPDDR6, HBM) package and platform requirements

Preferred Qualifications

  • 5+ years leading package or board development with a proven track record of defining multi-chiplet (2.5D/3D, EMIB, fan-out) architectures
  • Extensive experience defining package substrate stack-ups, selecting materials, managing netlists, and creating optimized pinouts and ball maps
  • Knowledge of board and platform design is an added advantage
  • Hands-on proficiency with Cadence APD / SiP Layout or Mentor Graphics Xpedition (Xpedition Substrate Integrator)
  • Experience leading cross-functional package workgroups, managing dependencies, and driving predictable execution through effective communication, clear decision-making, and timely escalation

Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As a Packaging Module Development Engineer, you will play an essential role in developing innovative advanced packaging processes and equipment that ensure Intel's competitive edge in semiconductor manufacturing. Your daily responsibilities will focus on optimizing assembly methods to meet quality, reliability, cost, and efficiency targets in high-volume production environments. By collaborating with cross-functional teams, your contributions will directly support Intel's advancements in next-generation packaging technologies.

Business Group
This position is part of Intel Corporation's Substrate Packaging Technology Development (SPTD) organization, which specializes in driving innovations to enable heterogeneous integration and die disaggregation across Intel's product portfolio. The group focuses on delivering scalable packaging solutions to address high-performance and mobile computing applications, supporting Intel's global technology leadership.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and optimize advanced packaging processes, materials, and equipment to achieve reliability, cost, and quality targets.
  • Define and implement process specifications, workflows, and equipment configurations for new technologies.
  • Conduct design of experiments (DOE) to characterize process windows and evaluate interactions among equipment, materials, and chemistry.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance process capability, stability, yield, and productivity.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to address technical challenges and deliver impactful solutions.
  • Establish material specifications and partner with suppliers to ensure quality and performance compliance.
  • Document advancements and process innovations through technical reports and presentations.
  • Provide ongoing support for equipment performance and process health in high-volume production environments.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience would be obtained through a combination of prior education level classes, and current level school classes, projects, research and relevant previous job and/or internship experience.

Minimum Qualifications:

To be initially considered for this position, candidates must meet one of the following education and experience thresholds:

  • Ph.D. in Optical Engineering, Optics, Photonics, Physics, Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, or a related STEM field (recent graduates with academic lab/dissertation research in laser processing, optics, or laser-material interaction are strongly encouraged to apply); OR Master's degree in the above STEM disciplines with 1+ years of relevant experience (which may include graduate thesis research, academic lab projects, or industry internships); OR Bachelor's degree in the above STEM disciplines with 3+ years of relevant industry experience in laser processing, precision equipment engineering, or semiconductor manufacturing.
  • Relevant experience will be any of the following:
    • Working with laser, optical, photonic, or related advanced processing technologies in a laboratory, manufacturing, or development environment.
    • Programming or scripting tools (e.g., Python, MATLAB, JMP/JSL, C++, LabVIEW) for data analysis, process development, automation, or equipment control.
    • Applying experimental methods (DOE), statistical analysis, and data-driven problem-solving to technical challenges.
    • Applying experimental methods, statistical analysis, and data-driven problem-solving to technical challenges.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of:
    • Developing laser, optical test, or precision micromachining processes for semiconductor, microelectronics, advanced materials, or related applications.
    • Laser-material interactions (e.g., ultrafast pulse dynamics, non-linear optical absorption, thermal vs. athermal ablation regimes, or laser-assisted surface finishing).
    • JMP Scripting Language (JSL) or custom scripting for automated reporting, coordinate translation, toolpath generation, or recipe automation.
    • 3D optical profilers, confocal microscopes, or surface metrology tools to evaluate micro-features, step heights, and surface roughness.
    • Optical modeling tools or multi-physics simulation software (e.g., COMSOL, ANSYS) for thermal or optical-mechanical modeling.

descriptionHtml:

As a SoC Functional Validation Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring the quality and reliability of Intel's cutting-edge System-on-Chip (SoC) solutions. You will be responsible for validating and verifying the functionality of complex SoC designs in the pre-silicon phase to meet stringent industry standards. Working closely with cross-functional teams, you will debug issues, develop test plans, and execute validation processes to deliver high-performing products that drive innovation in the semiconductor industry.

- Execute validation processes using industry-standard tools and methodologies.
- Debug issues at the hardware and software interface levels to ensure functionality and performance requirements are met.
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including design and architecture, to identify and resolve validation challenges.
- Create and maintain documentation for validation processes, test cases, and results.
- Analyze root causes of validation failures and propose solutions to improve overall design quality.

title: PDK Engineer Extraction Development
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As a Process Design Kit (PDK) Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in developing and ensuring the quality of PDK collateral that enables cutting-edge silicon designs. You will be responsible for maintaining and validating design environments for specific technology nodes, working on parasitic extraction, physical verification, and design methodologies to set the foundation for high-quality, efficient design flows. This role is integral to advancing Intel's product lines and ensuring seamless collaboration across design and manufacturing teams.

Business Group
You will join the Design Technology Platform Enablement group, which focuses on creating world-class design environments to support Intel's advanced process technologies. This group collaborates with design teams, EDA vendors, and technology development experts to deliver high-quality design tools and methodologies that drive innovation across Intel's product offerings.
Key Responsibilities
- Develop and maintain PDK collateral, with focus on Parasitic Extraction (PEX) collateral, including Metal R and C extraction, LVS runsets and techfiles.
- Build test structures and simulate physical verification, parasitic extraction, and device modeling to deliver high-quality design solutions.
- Collaborate with stakeholders to resolve PDK-related issues, including debugging, root cause analysis, and error dispositioning.
- Drive automation and scalability by developing QA methodologies and tools to enhance coverage across technology nodes.
- Partner with EDA vendors to enable new tool functionalities and improve design workflows.
- Document and deliver design flows, guidelines, and tutorials to optimize usability for internal and external design communities.
- Engage with cross-functional teams to support new process development and ensure ease of use for the design ecosystem.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field, with 6+ years of experience in PDK development and validation; OR Master's degree with 4+ years of experience; OR Ph.D. with 2+ years of experience.
- Hands-on expertise in physical verification tools and parasitic extraction tools (e.g., Calibre, Pegasus, ICV, StarRC, QRC).
- Strong programming and scripting skills in languages such as Python, TCL, or Perl for automation and workflow optimization.
- Proven experience with advanced technology nodes, including physical design verification and device modeling.

Preferred Qualifications
- Foundational understanding of CMOS device physics, semiconductor process technologies, and design rules.
- Familiarity with reliability verification techniques, including EM/IR flows and concepts.
- Exposure and working experience with AI tools and LLMs
- Strong organizational, presentation, and communication skills to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and vendors.

title: Failure Analysis Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

As a Manufacturing Failure Analysis Engineer, you play a critical role in ensuring the quality, reliability, and manufacturability of Intel's advanced silicon, package, platform, and board technologies. Your work focuses on identifying, isolating, and resolving failures across a broad portfolio of packaging technologies, ranging from Client and Server products to legacy and next-generation architectures, including FCBGA, LGA, Multiple Chip Packaging (MCP), molded packages, Foveros, and EMIB technologies.


You collaborate closely with customers, factory stakeholders, virtual factory teams, upstream process partners, including DSDP, Wafer Level Assembly (WLA), bumping operations, and Technology Development organizations to drive effective problem-solving, root cause investigations, and continuous process improvements. Through comprehensive failure analysis and data-driven decision making, you help optimize yield, quality, and product reliability across the manufacturing network.


Leveraging a wide range of laboratory and analytical tools, from foundational techniques such as X-ray inspection, curve tracing, iTDR, IRLC measurements, and Keyence microscopy to advanced characterization methods including SEM, FIB, FTIR, and 3D X-ray analysis, you develop innovative methodologies to accelerate learning and defect isolation. By integrating automation, data analytics, and AI-driven solutions into daily operations, you continuously improve efficiency, accuracy, and overall failure analysis capability, directly contributing to Intel's ability to deliver high-performance products in a highly competitive semiconductor industry.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead failure analysis investigations for silicon, package, platform, and board technologies to improve manufacturing yield, product quality, and reliability.
  • Develop and execute comprehensive failure analysis strategies, including electrical, mechanical, and material characterization to identify root causes.
  • Investigate complex material-device interactions and process-related defects using advanced analytical and diagnostic techniques.
  • Create and enhance electrical, analytical, and mechanical methodologies to strengthen failure analysis capabilities for future technologies and advanced packaging solutions.
  • Support new technology introduction (NTI), product transfer activities, manufacturing startup, and automation initiatives that improve operational efficiency and diagnostic accuracy.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams across factories, virtual factories, technology development organizations, and suppliers to drive effective corrective and preventive actions.
  • Analyze failure trends, generate technical reports, and recommend process improvements to prevent recurrence while promoting knowledge sharing and best practices across global sites.
  • Leverage data analytics, machine learning, and AI-based solutions to improve problem-solving effectiveness, accelerate root cause identification, and enhance overall engineering productivity.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Microelectronics, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, or a related discipline, with 2+ years of relevant hands-on experience acquired through industry roles, internships, research projects, academic coursework, or laboratory work; or a Master's degree in a related field with equivalent technical competency.
  • Solid understanding of failure analysis principles, methodologies, and diagnostic techniques ( failure isolation) , including electrical, mechanical, and material characterization.
  • Strong technical foundation in evaluating and troubleshooting the electrical and mechanical behavior of semiconductor devices, packages, and systems.
  • Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate complex technical issues and identify root causes using data-driven approaches.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills in English, with the ability to clearly present technical findings to diverse audiences.
  • Experience leading continuous improvement initiatives, process optimization projects, or cross-functional problem-solving activities.
  • Proven ability to collaborate effectively within multicultural and multidisciplinary teams in a fast-paced manufacturing or engineering environment.
  • Leadership experience or demonstrated capability to influence stakeholders and drive alignment across multiple organizations.
  • Experience leveraging AI, automation, data analytics, or machine learning tools to improve engineering productivity, quality, operational efficiency, and learning effectiveness.
  • Familiarity with advanced semiconductor packaging technologies and manufacturing processes is an added advantage.

Responsibilities will include but are not limited to: • Leads the estimate development from as Intel representative in working with internal customer and external supplier base • Sponsoring Intel 3rd Party Quantity Surveyor in driving accurate quantity measures and local market cost benchmarking in Intel Projects. • Driving process improvements. • Influencing cost reduction cash savings opportunities from Estimation standpoint. • Partner with Procurement team on various commercial activities such as Request For Proposal (RFP) to ensure optimized cost for construction projects. • Provides varying levels of advice and cost information to operational business groups or factories to drive the business decision-making process. • Provides information and counsel in the areas of controls/risk management, claims mitigation, budgeting and planning, pricing, cost, marketing strategies, return on investment decisions, and the development of overall business plans and strategies. • Interprets information for and negotiates with clients and customers both internal and external to the organization. • Provides input to management including department heads, operational managers, other departments, and senior management.

title: Facilities Chemical/Gas System Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

As a Facilities Chemical/Gas Systems Engineer, you will play a key role in ensuring the reliability, efficiency, and safety of Intel's factory support equipment infrastructure. You will manage system operations, resolve technical challenges, and provide engineering expertise to support manufacturing and facility objectives. Your contributions will directly impact Intel's ability to maintain its cutting-edge semiconductor fabrication processes and achieve operational excellence.

Business group

Facilities is at the heart of Intel's operations, creating an environment where employees thrive while driving the innovation that makes amazing technologies possible. Facilities is responsible for maintaining Intel's global sites, offices, labs, and factories, ensuring they operate efficiently and sustainably. The team is committed to environmental stewardship and supports Intel's ongoing initiatives to reduce energy use, waste generation, and greenhouse gas emissions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide engineering expertise for factory support equipment (i.e. Vacuum pumps, abatement units, heat exchanger) to ensuring operational reliability and compliance with semiconductor requirements.
  • Manage system troubleshooting, preventive maintenance, and capacity planning to meet operational demands.
  • Develop and maintain standard operating procedures and ensure compliance with safety and regulatory standards.
  • Manage project scopes, budgets, schedules, and commissioning for factory support equipment installations and upgrades.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, suppliers, and stakeholders to deliver cost-effective solutions that meet design criteria.
  • Support construction and operations teams through effective coordination and field oversight.
  • Create and maintain documentation, including installation procedures, commissioning checklists, and sequence of operations.

Behavioral traits:

  • Organizational, communication, and leadership skills.
  • Collaborate effectively across diverse teams and influence stakeholders.

Qualifications:

You must possess the requirements below to be considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. This position is not eligible for Intel Immigration Sponsorship

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Chemistry, or related field with 1 year of hands-on experience in chemical/gas systems through internships, academic projects, coursework, or hands-on training OR a Master's Degree in Engineering, Chemistry, or related field with no prior professional experience.
  • Experienced mentioned above should a combination of the following areas:
    • Chemical compatibility, high-purity gases, and process control statistical analysis.
    • Materials of construction for chemical and gas systems infrastructure.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with vacuum pumps, point-of-use abatement systems, chillers, and heat exchangers.
  • Hands-on experience in startup and commissioning of facilities systems.

If you are passionate about solving complex engineering challenges and want to contribute to Intel's success in a meaningful way, we encourage you to apply and be part of our journey to innovate and inspire.

title: Module Engineer within Test Engineering Department
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact As a Module Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in managing and optimizing high-volume manufacturing equipment and processes that enable the production of advanced integrated circuits. You will conduct thorough tests, recommend and implement improvements, and support technology transfers to ensure manufacturing excellence. Your contributions will drive device miniaturization, enhance product quality, and boost the production efficiency of Intel's cutting-edge technologies. Business Group Intel Corporation's Assembly Engineering group is dedicated to enabling world-class semiconductor manufacturing through innovative technology development and high-volume production. The team focuses on advancing manufacturing processes, supporting technology transfers, and contributing to Intel's mission of creating world-changing technology that improves lives globally. Key Responsibilities - Manage critical high-volume manufacturing equipment and processes to support device miniaturization and integrated circuit production. - Conduct tests and measurements to ensure control over critical dimensions and defectivity within the production line. - Implement modifications to optimize production techniques and improve manufacturing efficiencies. - Execute maintenance and repair activities for equipment and relevant module components. - Drive continuous improvement initiatives focusing on safety, quality, cost, productivity, and yield metrics. - Collaborate with equipment suppliers to resolve technical issues and implement improvements. - Develop and optimize systems to prevent excursions and detect discrepancies in materials and equipment processes. - Participate in technology transfer activities to ensure consistent processing standards across global manufacturing sites. - Lead equipment installation, conversion, and qualification during factory ramps, ensuring safety, quality, and schedule adherence.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications - Bachelor's degree in Electronics, Electrical, Automation Control, or other relevant engineering fields, with 0-1 years of hands-on experience in domain gained through internships, academic projects, coursework, or hands-on training; OR a Master's degree in relevant fields with no prior professional experience. - Knowledge of schematic/electronic circuitry interpretation. - Proficiency in using MS Office applications, including Outlook, Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. - Willingness to work onsite in a 12-hour rotational shift pattern, 4 days per week, as required by business needs. Preferred Qualifications - Experience with data analysis using programming languages such as SQL, Python, or R. - Familiarity with industry-standard Tester and Handler Equipment (ATE) and Test Programs. - Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail. - Ability to work collaboratively within team-oriented environments. - Prior experience in the semiconductor industry or high-volume manufacturing settings is an advantage. Join our team to contribute to groundbreaking innovations, collaborate globally, and grow personally and professionally. Your role will be integral to advancing Intel's manufacturing capabilities and shaping the future of technology.
